74636.e: In the slide master you set the font, colours, logo and layout in one place. A change there affects all the slides.
74636.m: The slide master sets the look of all slides.

74637.q: What do you call the effect that plays when changing from one slide to the next?
74637.e: A slide transition affects the whole slide when it changes, for example a fade. An animation, on the other hand, moves individual objects on a slide.
74637.m: A slide transition is the effect when changing slides.

74638.q: What does presenter view show during a presentation?
a: Notes that only the speaker can see
All slides at once for the audience
The names of the people watching
The spelling mistakes in the presentation
74638.e: In presenter view, the speaker sees their notes, the next slide and the time. The audience only sees the current slide.
74638.m: In presenter view, only the speaker sees their notes.

74639.q: Which rule makes sense for text on presentation slides?
a: A few key words instead of long paragraphs
As much text as possible in small print
Every line in a different colour
The whole talk word for word
74639.e: The audience should listen and not spend a long time reading. Short key words and easy-to-read text support the talk.
74639.m: Good slides show only a few key words.

74640.q: Which key starts the slide show from the beginning in many presentation programs?
74640.e: In PowerPoint, F5 starts the presentation from the first slide. You end it again with Esc.
74640.m: You start a presentation with F5.

74641.q: Which device is often used to project a presentation onto the wall in the classroom?
74641.e: A projector (video projector) throws the computer's picture, enlarged, onto a screen or wall.
74641.m: A projector puts the computer picture onto the wall.

74642.q: Which colour combination is usually easiest to read on slides?
a: Dark text on a light background
Red text on a green background
Yellow text on a white background
Light blue text on a grey background
74642.e: A strong contrast between text and background makes text easy to read. Red on green is also hard to make out for people with red-green colour blindness.
74642.m: A strong contrast makes slides easy to read.

74643.q: What do quotation marks around several words do in a search engine?
a: It searches for exactly this sequence of words
74643.e: With quotation marks, for example "Rhine at Basel", the search engine looks for pages with exactly this sequence of words.
74643.m: Quotation marks search for an exact sequence of words.

74644.q: What does a minus sign directly in front of a search term do, for example jaguar -car?
a: Pages with this word are excluded
The word is given extra weight
74644.e: The minus sign excludes results with the word that follows. That way you are more likely to find pages about the animal than about the car brand.
74644.m: With a minus sign you exclude words from the search.

74645.q: What does the search operator site:admin.ch do together with a search term?
a: The page is saved as a favourite
Only pictures from this site are shown
74645.e: With site: you limit the search to a particular website or domain, here to the pages of the Swiss federal administration.
74645.m: The site operator limits the search to a single website.

74646.q: Which search operator lets you find PDF documents on a topic?
74646.e: The operator filetype: limits the results to one file type. That way you can find fact sheets or reports in PDF format, for example.
74646.m: The filetype operator finds files of a particular type.

74647.q: Where on a website do you usually find out who is responsible for the content?
74647.e: The legal notice names the operator of a website with name and address. This helps you judge how trustworthy a source is.
74647.m: The legal notice says who is behind a website.

74648.q: What is the program called that automatically searches and records web pages for a search engine?
74648.e: A web crawler follows links from page to page and collects their content. From this the search engine builds its index.
74648.m: A web crawler searches the web for a search engine.

74649.q: How can you usually recognise paid entries in search results?
a: By a label such as “Ad” or “Sponsored”
By the fact that they are always at the very bottom
By the fact that they have no link
74649.e: Search engines often show paid advertising above the normal results. It is marked with labels such as “Ad” or “Sponsored”.
74649.m: Paid search results are labelled as ads.

74650.q: What is a good strategy for checking information found on the internet?
a: Compare it with several reliable sources
Only look at the number of likes
Choose the page with the most pictures
74650.e: If several independent and reliable sources report the same thing, information is more believable. A single result can be wrong or out of date.
74650.m: Check important information in several sources.

74651.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
74651.e: The British physicist Tim Berners-Lee developed the World Wide Web at the end of the 1980s. He wanted to use it to share research data easily.
74651.m: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web.

74652.q: At which research centre in Switzerland did the World Wide Web come into being?
74652.e: Tim Berners-Lee was working at CERN near Geneva when he wrote his proposal for the web in 1989. The first website also went online there.
74652.m: The World Wide Web was invented at CERN in Geneva.

74653.q: In which language is the structure of web pages described?
74653.e: HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) uses tags to set what on a page is a heading, a paragraph, a picture or a link.
74653.m: Web pages are described with HTML.

74654.q: What do you call a program that displays web pages?
74654.e: A browser loads web pages from the internet and displays them. Well-known browsers are Firefox, Chrome, Safari and Edge.
74654.m: You look at web pages with a browser.

74655.q: What do you call a clickable word or picture that leads to another web page?
74655.e: Hyperlinks connect web pages with each other. This network of links gave rise to the name “web”.
74655.m: Hyperlinks connect web pages with each other.

74656.q: How are the internet and the World Wide Web connected?
a: The web is a service that uses the internet
The internet and the web are exactly the same
The internet is part of the web
The web is older than the internet
74656.e: The internet is the worldwide network of connected computers. The web is one of its services, like email or video calling.
74656.m: The World Wide Web is just one service of the internet.

74657.q: When did the forerunner of today's internet come into being?
74657.e: In 1969, the first computers at universities in the USA were connected into a network. The internet later developed from this.
74657.m: The forerunner of the internet came into being in 1969.

74658.q: Which country ending do internet addresses from Switzerland have?
74658.e: .ch stands for “Confoederatio Helvetica”, the Latin name of Switzerland. .cz, on the other hand, is the ending for the Czech Republic.

74659.q: What do you call the full address of a web page, for example https://www.admin.ch?
74659.e: URL stands for “Uniform Resource Locator”. It says where a resource is on the internet and how to fetch it.
74659.m: The address of a web page is called a URL.

74660.q: How many numbers separated by dots make up an IPv4 address?
74660.e: An IPv4 address such as 192.168.1.20 is made up of four numbers separated by dots.
74660.m: An IPv4 address is made up of four numbers.

74661.q: What is the biggest number that may appear in one part of an IPv4 address?
74661.e: Each of the four parts is 8 bits in size. This makes the values 0 to 255 possible.
74661.m: Each part of an IPv4 address is between 0 and 255.

74662.q: Which of the following IPv4 addresses is valid?
74662.e: A valid IPv4 address has exactly four numbers from 0 to 255. 300 is too big, and the others have too few or too many parts.
74662.m: A valid IPv4 address has four numbers from 0 to 255.

74663.q: Which of these IP addresses is a private address, as is usual in home networks?
74663.e: The ranges 10.x.x.x, 172.16.x.x to 172.31.x.x and 192.168.x.x are reserved for private networks. Such addresses are not passed on directly on the internet.
74663.m: Addresses beginning with 192.168 are private addresses.

a: Because IPv4 addresses were running out
Because IPv4 does not allow numbers
Because IPv4 only applied in Europe
74664.e: IPv4 offers about 4.3 billion addresses. With billions of devices worldwide, that is no longer enough, which is why there is IPv6.
74664.m: IPv6 solves the problem of IPv4 addresses running out.

74665.q: Which character separates the blocks of an IPv6 address?
74665.e: An IPv6 address is made up of eight blocks of hexadecimal numbers, for example 2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:1. The blocks are separated by colons.
74665.m: In IPv6, colons separate the individual blocks.

74666.q: Where does a mobile phone in a home network usually get its IP address from?
a: You have to make it up yourself
It is printed on the battery
From the printer in the network
74666.e: The router hands out the IP addresses in the home network automatically. When a device connects, it immediately gets a free address.
74666.m: In a home network, the router hands out IP addresses automatically.

74667.q: Which computer does the special IP address 127.0.0.1 stand for?
a: The biggest server in the world
74667.e: 127.0.0.1 is also called “localhost”. With this address a computer talks to itself, for example to test programs.
74667.m: The address 127.0.0.1 always means your own computer.

74668.q: What does the abbreviation WLAN stand for?
74668.e: WLAN means “wireless local area network”. Devices connect through it by radio instead of by cable.
74668.m: A WLAN is a wireless local network.

74669.q: What do you usually need to connect to someone else's protected Wi-Fi?
74669.e: Protected Wi-Fi networks ask for a password. Only people who know it can connect and use the internet.
74669.m: A protected Wi-Fi network needs a password.

74670.q: How does a Wi-Fi router send data to your mobile phone?
a: With light beams from a lamp
74670.e: A Wi-Fi router sends and receives radio waves. That is why no cable is needed between the router and the phone.
74670.m: Wi-Fi transmits data with radio waves.

74672.q: Which of the following Wi-Fi security standards is the newest?
74672.e: WPA3 was introduced in 2018 and is the successor to WPA2. The old WEP is considered easy to crack and should no longer be used.
74672.m: WPA3 is the current security standard for Wi-Fi.

74673.q: What do you call a public Wi-Fi access point, for example at a railway station?
74673.e: A hotspot offers wireless internet access in public. A smartphone can also serve as a personal hotspot.
74673.m: A public Wi-Fi access point is called a hotspot.

74674.q: Which term is mostly used in English-speaking countries for WLAN?
74674.e: In English people mostly say Wi-Fi. The name belongs to the Wi-Fi Alliance, which certifies devices to the WLAN standard IEEE 802.11.
74674.m: In English, WLAN is mostly called Wi-Fi.

74675.q: What weakens the Wi-Fi signal in a flat especially strongly?
74675.e: Radio waves are strongly weakened by concrete and metal. That is why reception behind several thick walls is often poor.
74675.m: Thick concrete walls weaken the Wi-Fi signal.

74676.q: What does it mean to save data “in the cloud”?
a: It is kept on servers on the internet
It is only on the USB stick
It is in the computer's working memory
74676.e: With the cloud, data is stored in a provider's data centres. You access it over the internet.
74676.m: In the cloud, data is kept on servers on the internet.

74677.q: What is a big advantage of cloud storage?
a: You can access the data from different devices
The data can be fetched anywhere without internet
The storage space is always unlimited and free
74677.e: Because the data is online, you can open it equally on a phone, tablet and computer.
74677.m: Cloud data is available on many devices.

74678.q: What do you usually need to access data in the cloud?
74678.e: Cloud services are reached over the internet. Without a connection, only files that were loaded onto the device beforehand are available.
74678.m: For the cloud you need internet.

74679.q: What is a building called in which very many servers for cloud services stand?
74679.e: In data centres, thousands of servers run around the clock. They are cooled and protected against failures with emergency power.
74679.m: Cloud data is kept in data centres.

74680.q: What does “Software as a Service” mean?
a: You use a program over the internet instead of installing it
You buy software on a CD in a shop
You repair broken software for money
74680.e: With Software as a Service (SaaS), the program runs at the provider. You use it, for example, directly in the browser, often with a subscription.
74680.m: With Software as a Service, the program runs on the internet.

74681.q: What happens when syncing with a cloud storage service?
a: Changes are matched up on all connected devices
All files are deleted for good
74681.e: If you change a file on one device, the new version is also transferred to the other devices via the cloud.
74681.m: Syncing keeps files up to date everywhere.

74682.q: What should you pay attention to before saving personal data in a cloud service?
a: How the provider protects the data
What colour the provider's logo is
How many adverts the provider shows
Whether the provider also sells printers
74682.e: In the cloud, data is kept by another company. That is why it is worth checking how it protects the data and whether it keeps to data protection rules.
74682.m: If you put data in the cloud, pay attention to the provider's data protection.

74683.q: What does a document shared in the cloud make possible for a group?
a: Several people can work on it at the same time
Only one person can ever open it
The document can never be changed again
74683.e: With shared online documents, everyone involved sees changes almost immediately. That way a class can work on a text together.
74683.m: In the cloud you can work on a document together.

74684.q: What is a safety copy of data called in English?
74684.e: A backup is a copy of important data. If the original is lost, you can restore the data from it.
74684.m: A backup is a safety copy.

74685.q: What does the 3-2-1 rule of data backup say?
a: 3 copies, on 2 kinds of storage media, 1 of them in another place
Back up for 3 days, wait for 2 days, delete on 1 day
74685.e: You keep three copies of the data, use two different storage media and store one copy away from home. That way you can survive even a fire or theft.
74685.m: According to the 3-2-1 rule, one copy of the data is kept in another place.

74686.q: Why does a backup often only copy the files that have changed since last time?
a: It is faster and needs less space
Because you must never back up old files
So that the files become more colourful
74686.e: Unchanged files are already in the last backup. If you only copy new and changed files, you save time and storage space.
74686.m: Backing up only changes saves time and space.

74687.q: What is a backup called in which all the data is copied completely every time?
74687.e: In a full backup, all the selected data is copied completely. It needs the most time and storage space.
74687.m: A full backup copies all the data.

74688.q: What does a regular backup protect against in a ransomware attack?
a: Against permanently losing the encrypted data
Against any infection of the computer
Against spam emails in the inbox
74688.e: Ransomware encrypts data and demands a ransom. With a backup kept separately, you can restore the data without paying.
74688.m: A separate backup helps against blackmail with ransomware.

74689.q: Why should an external backup hard drive be disconnected from the computer after the backup?
a: So that viruses or faults do not damage it too
So that it gets more storage
So that the computer starts faster
74689.e: If the backup stays connected all the time, malware can also attack the backup. Kept separately, it stays protected.
74689.m: Keep a backup separate from the computer.

74690.q: What should you check from time to time after making a backup?
a: Whether the data can really be restored
Whether the backup has a nice colour
74690.e: A backup is only useful if restoring works. That is why you test from time to time whether you can get files back.
74690.m: A backup is only good if restoring it works.

74691.q: What do you call getting data back from a backup?
74691.e: When restoring, backed-up files are copied back to their place.
74691.m: You get data back from a backup by restoring it.

74692.q: In the Caesar cipher, every letter is shifted 3 places along the alphabet. What does HELLO become?
74692.e: Every letter moves on 3 places: H becomes K, E becomes H, L becomes O and O becomes R. This gives KHOOR.
74692.m: In the Caesar cipher you shift every letter by the same amount.

74693.q: A word was shifted by 3 places with the Caesar cipher and now reads WUHH. What was the original word?
74693.e: To decrypt, you shift each letter back 3 places: W becomes T, U becomes R and H becomes E.
74693.m: To decrypt, you shift the letters back.

74694.q: What do you call a message before it is encrypted?
74694.e: The readable original text is called plaintext. After encryption it becomes unreadable ciphertext.

74695.q: What is typical of symmetric encryption?
a: The same key is used to encrypt and decrypt
No key is used at all
Each person has a public and a private key
The text is just written backwards
74695.e: In symmetric methods, sender and receiver have the same secret key. The Caesar cipher is a simple example of this.
74695.m: Symmetric encryption uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt.

74696.q: Which two keys belong to asymmetric encryption?
a: A public key and a private key
A big key and a small key
An old key and a new key
A house key and a car key
74696.e: Anyone may encrypt with the public key. Only someone who has the matching private key can decrypt.
74696.m: In asymmetric encryption there is a public and a private key.

74697.q: What does the “S” in HTTPS show?
a: That the site comes from Switzerland
That the site loads especially fast
That the site only contains games
74697.e: HTTPS stands for “Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure”. The data between the browser and the website is sent encrypted.
74697.m: HTTPS means an encrypted connection to the website.

74698.q: What was the name of the German armed forces' cipher machine in the Second World War, whose code was cracked at Bletchley Park?
74698.e: The German military encrypted its radio messages with the Enigma. Experts at Bletchley Park, including Alan Turing, were able to decrypt many of them.
74698.m: The Enigma was a famous cipher machine.

74798.q: Who should always go with small children near water?
74798.e: Small children can drown quickly and very quietly. That is why they should only be near water with an adult.
74798.m: Small children only go near water with adults.

74799.q: How close should a small child be to the person watching them by the water?
74799.e: The person watching should be able to grab a small child immediately. So the child should be within arm's reach, only a few steps away.
74799.m: Small children stay within arm's reach near water.

74800.q: What should you do if you are very hot and want to go into the water?
74800.e: The body needs time to get used to cold water. That is why you never jump into the water when you are overheated.
74800.m: If you are hot, cool down before going into the water.

74801.q: How should your tummy be when you go swimming?
a: Not too full and not too empty
74801.e: One water safety rule says you should never swim with a full or completely empty stomach. Both can weaken the body.
74801.m: Don't go swimming with a very full or completely empty stomach.

74802.q: Where may you play with an airbed and armbands?
a: Only where you can still stand
In the middle of a deep lake
74802.e: Airbeds and swimming aids can drift away or lose air. In deep water they don't keep you safe.
74802.m: Swimming aids don't protect you in deep water.

74803.q: How do you swim a long distance in a lake safely?
74803.e: Even good swimmers can suddenly get tired or get cramp. That is why you never swim long distances alone.

74804.q: Which organisation in Switzerland set out the well-known water safety rules?
74804.e: The SLRG is the Swiss Lifesaving Society. It works to make sure fewer people drown.
74804.m: The SLRG helps prevent accidents in the water with its water safety rules.

74805.q: How many water safety rules does the SLRG have?
74805.e: The SLRG has six water safety rules. They help people stay safe in swimming pools, lakes and rivers.
74805.m: The SLRG has six water safety rules.

74806.q: How do small children usually drown?
74806.e: Children who are drowning often can no longer call out or wave. That is why people sometimes don't notice, and you always have to watch carefully.

74807.q: How many tasks are there in the Water Safety Check?
74807.e: The Water Safety Check has three tasks. You do them one after the other without a break.
74807.m: The Water Safety Check has three tasks.

74808.q: How do you get into the deep water in the Water Safety Check?
a: By rolling in from the side of the pool
74808.e: In the first task you roll or tumble from the side of the pool into deep water. This practises keeping your sense of direction after falling into water.
74808.m: In the Water Safety Check you roll from the edge into deep water.

74809.q: How long do you have to stay afloat in one place in the Water Safety Check?
74809.e: After the roll you stay afloat in the same spot for one minute. You are not allowed to swim away.
74809.m: In the Water Safety Check you stay afloat for one minute.

74810.q: How far do you swim in the Water Safety Check?
74810.e: The last task is to swim 50 metres and then climb out of the water.
74810.m: In the Water Safety Check you swim 50 metres.

74811.q: What do you have to do at the very end of the Water Safety Check?
74811.e: After the 50 metres you have to climb out of the pool on your own. This is also part of being able to save yourself.
74811.m: Climbing out of the water is part of the Water Safety Check.

74812.q: Are you allowed to take a break between the tasks of the Water Safety Check?
a: No, you do everything without a break
Yes, you can go and eat
74812.e: The three tasks follow straight after each other. That way it is like a real emergency in the water.
74812.m: The tasks of the Water Safety Check follow without a break.

74813.q: What do you get when you pass the Water Safety Check?
74813.e: Anyone who manages all three tasks gets a certificate card. It shows that you have passed the check.
74813.m: If you pass the Water Safety Check, you get a certificate card.

74814.q: Can a child swim without supervision after passing the Water Safety Check?
74814.e: The Water Safety Check shows that a child can save themselves in the water. Even so, children should never swim without supervision.
74814.m: Even after the Water Safety Check, you only swim with supervision.

74815.q: Where do many children in Switzerland do the Water Safety Check?
74815.e: Many schools carry out the Water Safety Check during swimming lessons. It is seen as the basis for safety in the water.
74815.m: Many children do the Water Safety Check at school.

74816.q: What colour must the front light on a bike be?
74816.e: At the front, a bike has a white or slightly yellow light. This lets people coming towards you see you.
74816.m: The front bike light is white.

74817.q: What colour must the rear light on a bike be?
74817.e: At the back, a bike has a red light. This lets the cars behind you see you.
74817.m: The rear bike light is red.

74818.q: What do you use on a bike to warn other people with a sound?
74818.e: In Switzerland a bike bell is part of the required equipment. You can use it to warn others.
74818.m: You warn others with the bike bell.

74819.q: What do you show by holding out your arm on a bike?
74819.e: Before turning, you hold your arm out in the direction you want to go. That way others know what you are planning.
74819.m: Before turning, you show the direction with your arm.

74820.q: How many brakes must a bike have in Switzerland?
74820.e: A bike needs one brake for the front wheel and one for the back wheel. That way you can stop safely.

74821.q: Where may children under 12 in Switzerland ride a bike if there is no cycle path?
74821.e: Since 2021, children under 12 have been allowed to ride on the pavement if there is no cycle path or cycle lane. They must be considerate of pedestrians.
74821.m: Children under 12 may ride on the pavement if there is no cycle path.

74822.q: Where should a bike helmet sit at the front?
a: Right at the back on the neck
On the back of the head
74822.e: A good helmet sits straight and covers the forehead. At the front it should be just above the eyebrows.
74822.m: The helmet covers the forehead to just above the eyebrows.

74823.q: How much space should there be between the chin strap and the chin?
74823.e: The chin strap should be tight but not pinch. About one or two fingers should fit in between.
74823.m: One or two fingers fit under the chin strap.

74824.q: What do you do with a bike helmet after a bad fall?
74824.e: After a hard impact the helmet may be damaged inside, even if you can't see anything. That is why you need a new helmet.
74824.m: After a bad fall you need a new helmet.

74825.q: Do you have to fasten your bike helmet when riding?
74825.e: An unfastened helmet can fall off your head in a crash. It only protects you properly when it is fastened.
74825.m: A helmet only protects you when it is fastened.

74826.q: What material is the inner shell of a bike helmet usually made of?
74826.e: Inside, the helmet has a layer of hard foam. It squashes together on impact and cushions the blow.
74826.m: The hard foam in the helmet cushions the impact.

74827.q: When else do children wear a helmet?
74827.e: You can also fall on a scooter, a skateboard or inline skates. That is why a helmet makes sense there too.
74827.m: A helmet also protects your head on a scooter.

74828.q: What is the wall made of lots of wooden bars that you can climb in the gym called?
74828.e: Wall bars are made of lots of horizontal wooden bars. You can climb them and hold on to them.
74828.m: In the gym you climb on the wall bars.

74829.q: What is the piece of equipment made of several wooden sections that can be stacked on top of each other called?
74829.e: The vaulting box is made of several wooden frames and a padded top. You can make it higher or lower by taking sections away.
74829.m: The vaulting box is put together from several sections.

74830.q: What is the long, narrow wooden bench in the gym called?
74830.e: The gym bench is a long wooden bench. You can sit on it, balance on it or turn it upside down.
74830.m: You can also balance on the gym bench.

74831.q: Which piece of equipment helps you take off so you can jump higher?
74831.e: The springboard bounces when you take off. That way you can jump over a vaulting box or buck, for example.
74831.m: The springboard helps you jump higher.

74832.q: What do you hang from in gymnastics, holding round grips on two ropes?
74832.e: The rings hang from the ceiling on two ropes. You can hang from them, swing and do exercises.
74832.m: The rings hang from the ceiling on ropes.

74833.q: What is the single horizontal metal bar used in gymnastics called?
74833.e: The horizontal bar is a single metal bar. You can hang from it, swing or pull yourself up.
74833.m: On the horizontal bar you do gymnastics on a single bar.

74834.q: What is the very thick, soft mat for jumps from a great height called?
74834.e: The crash mat is very thick and soft. It catches you gently when you jump.
74834.m: The crash mat is especially thick and soft.

74835.q: What is the piece of equipment with four legs and a padded top that you jump over called?
74835.e: The buck has four legs and a pad on top. You jump over it using your hands, for example with a straddle.
74835.m: You jump over the buck using your hands.

74836.q: What is usually said before the start of a race?
a: On your marks, get set, go
74836.e: At the start, the starter says “On your marks, get set, go”. In races there is often a bang instead of “go”.
74836.m: A race starts with “On your marks, get set, go”.

74837.q: What is the obstacle that runners jump over in a hurdles race called?
74837.e: In a hurdles race there are several hurdles on the track. You have to jump over them while running.
74837.m: In a hurdles race you jump over hurdles.

74838.q: What is the jump called in which you go over a bar placed high up?
74838.e: In the high jump you jump over a bar. Then you land on a thick mat.
74838.m: In the high jump you jump over a bar.

74839.q: In which event do you push a heavy metal ball?
74839.e: In the shot put the ball is pushed away from the neck. You are not allowed to throw it like a ball.
74839.m: In the shot put you push a heavy ball.

74840.q: What is the board you take off from in the long jump called?
74840.e: The take-off board is in front of the sandpit. Anyone who steps over the line has a foul jump.
74840.m: In the long jump you take off from the take-off board.

74841.q: Which throwing implement is a long pole with a point?
74841.e: The javelin is long and has a metal tip at the front. It must land tip first.
74841.m: The javelin is a long pole with a point.

74842.q: Which throwing implement is a flat, round disc?
74842.e: The discus is a flat disc. You throw it while spinning round.
74842.m: The discus is a flat round disc.

74843.q: What is the jump with three jumps in a row called?
74843.e: In the triple jump you do a hop, a step and then a jump into the sandpit.
74843.m: The triple jump is made up of three jumps in a row.

74844.e: Warming up prepares the body for exercise. That is why you do it at the start of a PE lesson.

74845.q: What gets warmer and more supple when you warm up?
74845.e: Light movement gets more blood flowing to the muscles. They become warm and stretchier.
74845.m: When you warm up, your muscles get warm.

74846.q: What does a good warm-up protect you from?
74846.e: Warm muscles and joints are better prepared. That way you are less likely to get injured during sport.
74846.m: Warming up helps to prevent injuries.

74847.q: What happens to your heartbeat when you warm up?
74847.e: When you warm up, you move more. That is why the heart beats faster and pumps more blood around the body.
74847.m: When you warm up, your heart beats faster.

74848.q: How do you start a good warm-up?
74848.e: You start warming up slowly, for example with easy jogging. Only then do you go faster.
74848.m: A warm-up starts easy and then gets faster.

74849.q: What do you usually feel when you are well warmed up?
74849.e: When you warm up, the body moves and produces heat. That is why you feel warm afterwards and may sweat a little.
74849.m: After warming up you feel warm.

74850.q: What do people often do after sport so the body can calm down?
a: Cool down with an easy jog
74850.e: After sport people often jog gently for a little longer. That way the body can slowly recover.
74850.m: After sport you jog gently to cool down.

74851.q: What is the game called in which you have to hit your opponents with the ball?
74851.e: In dodgeball each team tries to hit the players of the other team with the ball. Anyone who is hit has to go to the area behind the opponents.
74851.m: In dodgeball you hit your opponents with the ball.

74852.q: In football, what is the throw with both hands from the touchline called?
74852.e: When the ball goes over the touchline, there is a throw-in. You throw the ball back onto the pitch with both hands over your head.
74852.m: For a throw-in you throw the ball with both hands over your head.

74853.q: Which team wins a football match?
a: The team with the nicer shirts
74853.e: In football only goals count. Whoever has scored more goals at the end wins.
74853.m: In football the team with more goals wins.

74854.q: What do you usually play the ball with in volleyball?
74854.e: In volleyball you hit or play the ball over the net with your hands and arms.
74854.m: In volleyball you play the ball with your hands and arms.

74855.q: In football, what is the kick from the corner of the pitch called?
74855.e: When a defender plays the ball over their own goal line, there is a corner kick. It is often just called a corner.
74855.m: A corner kick is taken from the corner of the pitch.

74856.q: What do you hit the ball with in floorball?
a: With a racket with a net
74856.e: In floorball every player has a plastic stick. You use it to control and shoot the ball.
74856.m: In floorball you play with a stick.

74857.q: What is the game called in which you have to run around bases after throwing the ball?
74857.e: In Brennball a player throws the ball into the field and then runs around the bases. The other team tries to get the ball to the “burn” base quickly.
74857.m: In Brennball you run around the bases.

74859.q: How should you ski on the piste?
a: So that you can stop at any time
74859.e: One piste rule says you must adapt your speed to your ability. You should be able to stop or get out of the way at any time.
74859.m: On the piste you only go as fast as you can safely brake.

74860.q: Where should you not stop on the piste?
a: In narrow places or where you can't see well
At the edge of the piste
74860.e: Anyone who stops in narrow places or where it is hard to see cannot be seen by others. That is why you stop at the edge in a place that is easy to see.
74860.m: Only stop at the edge of the piste where you can be seen.

74861.q: Where should you walk if you go up or down the piste on foot?
a: At the edge of the piste
In the middle of the piste
74861.e: Anyone on foot should use the edge of the piste. That way you don't get in the way of skiers or put them in danger.
74861.m: On foot you walk at the edge of the piste.

74862.q: What must you do if someone has had an accident on the piste?
74862.e: Everyone is obliged to help at an accident. For example, you can make the accident site safe and get help.
74862.m: If there is an accident on the piste, you help.

74863.q: What do you do before you start down a piste or set off again after stopping?
74863.e: Before setting off, you look up and down the slope. That way you don't crash into anyone.
74863.m: Before setting off, you look up the slope.

74864.q: What must you keep when overtaking on the ski piste?
74864.e: You may overtake on the left or right, but always with enough distance. The person being overtaken needs room for their movements.
74864.m: When overtaking on the piste, keep enough distance.

74865.q: What must you tell the other people involved after a skiing accident?
74865.e: The last piste rule is about identification. Everyone involved in an accident or who saw it must give their name and address.
74865.m: After a skiing accident you give your name and address.

74866.q: What must you always pay attention to on the ski piste?
74866.e: One piste rule says you must pay attention to markings and signs. They warn of dangers or closed pistes, for example.
74866.m: On the piste you pay attention to the signs.

74867.q: What is the fair thing to do if you notice that you touched the ball last before it went out?
74867.e: Being fair means being honest, even if it is bad for your own team. That keeps the game fair.

74868.q: How do you treat the referee if you play fair?
74868.e: The referee makes sure the game follows the rules. Even if you disagree, you stay polite.
74868.m: You treat the referee with respect.

74869.q: What does a fair player do when a teammate makes a mistake?
74869.e: Everyone makes mistakes sometimes. A fair teammate gives encouragement instead of telling them off.
74869.m: When teammates make mistakes, you encourage them.

74870.q: What is not fair play when playing?
74870.e: Anyone who trips someone on purpose can hurt others. That is unfair and against the rules.
74870.m: Fouling on purpose is not fair play.

74871.q: How do you pick teams fairly in a PE lesson?
a: So that nobody is left out
74871.e: Fair teams are about equally strong. Nobody should feel left out.
74871.m: With fair teams nobody is left out.

74872.q: What does a fair player do when an opponent has fallen?
74872.e: Helping a fallen opponent up shows respect. That is part of fair play.
74872.m: You help a fallen opponent up.

74873.q: What is part of fair play when you win?
74873.e: Winners stay fair too if they don't laugh at the others or show off. You can be happy without making others feel small.

74874.q: Which drink is best for children during sport?
74874.e: Water quenches your thirst and has no sugar. That is why it is the best drink during sport.
74874.m: During sport, water is the best drink.

74875.q: Why do you need to drink during sport?
a: Because you lose water through sweating
74875.e: During sport you sweat and lose water. You need to give this water back to your body.
74875.m: If you sweat, you need to drink again.

74876.q: When should you drink during sport?
74876.e: When you are very thirsty, your body is already missing water. That is why you regularly drink small sips.
74876.m: During sport you drink before you get very thirsty.

74877.q: What is sweat for during sport?
74877.e: When sweat evaporates on the skin, the skin becomes cooler. That way the body doesn't overheat.

74878.q: What is the best way to drink during sport?
74878.e: Small sips are good for your stomach. It is better to drink a little more often.
74878.m: During sport you drink in small sips.

74879.q: When do you need to drink especially a lot during sport?
74879.e: In hot weather you sweat more. That is why you need more to drink then.
74879.m: In hot weather you drink more.

74880.q: What is the best thing to take with you for a sports day or a hike?
74880.e: With your own water bottle you can drink at any time. You can often refill it with water at a fountain.
74880.m: A water bottle belongs at every sports event.

74881.q: In which game do two teams pull on a long rope?
74881.e: In a tug of war, two teams pull on the two ends of a rope. The team that pulls the other team over a line wins.
74881.m: In a tug of war, two teams pull on a rope.

74882.q: What do you stand in during a sack race?
74882.e: In a sack race you climb into a sack and hop to the finish in it. It is a popular game on sports day.
74882.m: In a sack race you hop in a sack.

74883.q: What is a race on sports day called in which each child only runs part of the distance?
74883.e: In a relay several children run one after the other. Each one hands over to the next at the end of their part.
74883.m: In a relay each child runs one part of the distance.

74884.q: What do you balance on a spoon in an egg and spoon race?
74884.e: In an egg and spoon race you carry an egg on a spoon to the finish. If it falls off, you have to put it back on.
74884.m: In an egg and spoon race you carry an egg on a spoon.

74885.q: What do you wear for protection on a sunny sports day?
74885.e: A cap or hat protects your head from the sun. Sun cream is important too.
74885.m: On sunny sports days a cap protects you from the sun.

74886.q: What is the race called in which two children each have one leg tied together?
74886.e: In a three-legged race, one leg of each of two children is tied together. Together they then have three legs to run with.
74886.m: In a three-legged race two children run with one leg tied together.

74887.q: What do children often get at the end of sports day?
74887.e: At the end of sports day there is often a prize-giving. Many children get a certificate or a medal.
74887.m: On sports day there are often certificates.

74888.q: How long is a skipping rope when it is the right length and you stand on the middle of it?
a: The handles reach up to your armpits
The handles reach up to your knees
The handles reach down to the floor
The handles reach far above your head
74888.e: You stand with both feet on the middle of the rope. The handles should then reach to roughly just below your armpits.
74888.m: A skipping rope of the right length reaches up to your armpits.

74889.q: What is skipping with two long ropes that two people turn in opposite directions called?
74889.e: In Double Dutch, two people turn two long ropes in opposite directions. A third person jumps in the middle. Double Under, Criss Cross and Side Swing are jumps with your own rope.
74889.m: In Double Dutch you jump over two ropes.

74890.q: What is skipping called as a competitive sport?
74890.e: Skipping with tricks and competitions is called rope skipping. There are even Swiss championships for it.
74890.m: Skipping as a sport is called rope skipping.

74891.q: What is a jump called in which the rope passes under your feet twice?
74891.e: For a double under you jump so high that the rope goes under your feet twice.
74891.m: In a double under the rope turns twice per jump.

74892.q: Which part of your feet is best to land on when skipping?
74892.e: On the balls of your feet you land softly and springily. This protects your joints.
74892.m: When skipping you land on the balls of your feet.

74893.q: What is it called when you cross your arms with the rope in front of your body while skipping?
74893.e: In a cross jump you cross your arms in front of your body. The rope then forms a loop that you jump through.
74893.m: In a cross jump you cross your arms.

74894.q: What does skipping train especially well?
74894.e: Skipping needs strength in your legs, endurance and good timing. That is why it trains many skills.

74895.q: What do you mainly use to turn the rope when skipping?
74895.e: The rope is mainly turned from the wrists. The arms stay close to the body.
74895.m: You turn the rope from your wrists.

74896.e: In long-distance running you move for a long time without a break. This puts a particular demand on the heart, circulation and breathing.

74897.q: What is the training method called in which periods of effort and planned breaks alternate?
74897.e: In the interval method, short intense efforts are followed by breaks in which you only partly recover. With the continuous method, on the other hand, you run without a break.
74897.m: In interval training, effort and rest alternate.

74898.q: How long do you run for in the Cooper test?
74898.e: In the Cooper test you try to run as far as possible in 12 minutes. The distance shows how good your endurance is.

74900.q: Which exercise without equipment mainly strengthens the arms and chest?
74900.e: In a press-up you push your body away from the floor with your arms. This mainly works the chest muscles, triceps and shoulder muscles.
74900.m: Press-ups strengthen the arms, shoulders and chest.

74901.q: In which exercise do you hold your body straight, supported only on your forearms and toes?
74901.e: In the forearm plank, the core muscles have to keep the body straight. The exercise strengthens the stomach and back.
74901.m: The forearm plank strengthens the core muscles.

74902.q: Why shouldn't you hold your breath during strength exercises?
74902.e: When you hold your breath under strain, the pressure in your chest rises and your blood pressure shoots up. It is better to breathe out as you push.
74902.m: During strength exercises you keep breathing steadily.

74904.q: What does the reaction time measure at the start of a sprint?
a: Time from the starting gun to the first movement
Time from the finish until stopping
74904.e: The reaction time begins with the starting signal and ends when the sprinter moves in the starting blocks. Good sprinters react in about one to two tenths of a second.
74904.m: Reaction time is the time between the signal and the first movement.

74905.q: Below which reaction time is a start in athletics counted as a false start?
74905.e: According to the rules of World Athletics, a person cannot react to the gun faster than 0.1 seconds. A faster reaction counts as a false start.
74905.m: Anyone who reacts faster than a tenth of a second has made a false start.

74906.q: From which starting position do sprinters begin the 100 metres?
74906.e: In a crouch start, sprinters support themselves with their hands on the ground and press their feet into the starting blocks. This lets them accelerate powerfully.

74907.q: Over which distance did Swiss sprinter Mujinga Kambundji become indoor world champion in 2022?
74907.e: Mujinga Kambundji won gold over 60 m at the 2022 World Indoor Championships in Belgrade. She is one of Switzerland's most successful sprinters.
74907.m: Mujinga Kambundji became indoor world champion over 60 metres in 2022.

74908.q: Which muscle fibres are especially important for fast, explosive movements?
74908.e: Fast-twitch muscle fibres contract quickly and powerfully but tire fast. Good sprinters have lots of them.
74908.m: For sprints you need fast-twitch muscle fibres.

74909.q: Which two things determine running speed?
74909.e: Speed is stride length times the number of strides per second. Anyone who takes longer or quicker strides runs faster.
74909.m: You are fast if you take long and frequent strides.

74910.q: Which two parts make up flexibility?
74910.e: Joint mobility is about the range of movement of the joints, stretchability is about the muscles, tendons and ligaments. Together they make up flexibility.
74910.m: Flexibility is made up of joint mobility and stretchability.

74911.q: In which sport is very great flexibility especially important?
74911.e: In rhythmic gymnastics, gymnasts show splits and extreme stretch positions. Without great flexibility these elements are not possible.
74911.m: Rhythmic gymnasts need very great flexibility.

74912.q: At what stage of life is flexibility easiest to maintain and improve?
74912.e: Children are naturally very flexible. Without training, flexibility decreases with age, so it is worth starting early.
74912.m: You should train flexibility even as a child.

74913.q: What is the exercise called in which the legs are spread fully in a line on the floor?
74913.e: In the splits the legs lie stretched forwards and backwards or to the sides on the floor. It needs very good stretchability.
74913.m: You need lots of flexibility for the splits.

74914.q: What does the “sit and reach” test check, in which you sit with straight legs and reach forwards?
a: The flexibility of the back and the backs of the thighs
The jumping power of the legs
74914.e: The further you can reach beyond your feet, the more flexible your hips, back and hamstrings are.
74914.m: The sit and reach test measures flexibility.

74915.q: What can happen if a muscle is permanently shortened?
74915.e: A shortened muscle no longer lets the joint move fully in all directions. Regular movement and stretching help to prevent this.

74916.q: Why do you warm up before sport?
a: So the muscles are warm and injuries are less likely
So you are more tired afterwards
So your pulse stays at rest
74916.e: When you warm up, the temperature in your muscles rises, and your heart and circulation adjust to the effort. This lowers the risk of injury and improves performance.
74916.m: Warming up protects against injury and helps you perform better.

74917.q: Roughly how long should a normal warm-up last?
74917.e: A warm-up of about 10 to 20 minutes is usually enough to get the body ready. Too long would already make you tired.
74917.m: A good warm-up lasts about 10 to 20 minutes.

74918.q: What is the set of running exercises such as high knees and heel flicks, often done to warm up, called in German-speaking sport?
74918.e: The running ABC is made up of exercises such as high knees, heel flicks and skips. It warms you up and trains running technique at the same time.
74918.m: The running ABC is part of the warm-up in many sports.

74919.q: Why shouldn't there be a long break between warming up and the competition?
a: Because the body would cool down again
Because you would have too much strength
Because the muscles would get too warm
Because your pulse would stay too high
74919.e: The effect of warming up doesn't last long. After a long break, the muscles and circulation are almost as cold as before.
74919.m: After warming up, the competition should start as soon as possible.

74920.q: What is the easy jogging and calming down of the body after training called?
74920.e: During the cool-down you keep moving gently after the effort. This lets your pulse and breathing slowly calm down.
74920.m: Training is followed by the cool-down.

74921.q: What is a specific warm-up for a football match?
74921.e: In a specific warm-up you practise movements that happen in the sport. For football these are passes, dribbling and short sprints, for example. Jogging or star jumps are part of a general warm-up.
74921.m: A specific warm-up practises the movements of your own sport.

74922.q: How long do you typically hold a position when doing static stretching?
74922.e: In static stretching you hold a stretch position still for about 20 to 30 seconds. You should feel a pull, but no pain.
74922.m: In static stretching you hold the position for half a minute.

74923.q: What is stretching with controlled, swinging movements called?
74923.e: In dynamic stretching you move your arms or legs back and forth in a controlled way, for example with leg swings. This type fits well into a warm-up.
74923.m: Dynamic stretching uses controlled swinging movements.

74924.q: What should you feel when stretching?
74924.e: A slight pull shows that the muscle is being stretched. Pain is a warning sign, and then you should ease off the stretch.
74924.m: Stretching may pull, but it should not hurt.

74925.q: Which muscle do you stretch when you stand and pull your heel towards your bottom?
74925.e: When the heel is pulled towards the bottom, the knee is bent a lot. This stretches the quadriceps at the front of the thigh.
74925.m: With your heel at your bottom you stretch the front of the thigh.

74926.q: Which muscle is stretched when, in a lunge position, you press the heel of the straight back leg into the floor?
74926.e: In this position the back of the lower leg is stretched. This is how you stretch the calf muscle.
74926.m: Pressing your heel to the floor in a lunge position stretches the calf.

74927.q: Why shouldn't you bounce jerkily when stretching?
a: Because the muscle tenses up as a reflex
Because the muscle would fall asleep
74927.e: Jerky movements trigger the stretch reflex, and the muscle contracts. This can lead to strains.
74927.m: When stretching you move calmly and with control.

74928.q: Where is the pulse often measured?
74928.e: At the wrist, on the thumb side, there is an artery just under the skin. You can feel the pulse there with two fingers.
74928.m: You can easily feel your pulse at the wrist or neck.

74929.q: Roughly what is the resting heart rate of adults?
74929.e: At rest, an adult's heart usually beats about 60 to 80 times per minute. In children the resting heart rate is a little higher.
74929.m: The resting heart rate of adults is about 60 to 80 beats per minute.

74930.q: You count 18 pulse beats in 15 seconds. What is your pulse per minute?
74930.e: A minute has 4 times 15 seconds. So you work out 18 times 4, which makes 72 beats per minute.
74930.m: Pulse beats in 15 seconds times four gives the pulse per minute.

74931.q: After a sprint you count 25 pulse beats in 10 seconds. What is your pulse per minute?
74931.e: A minute has 6 times 10 seconds. So you work out 25 times 6, which makes 150 beats per minute.
74931.m: Pulse beats in 10 seconds times six gives the pulse per minute.

74932.q: Why do athletes with good endurance training often have a low resting heart rate?
a: Their heart pumps more blood with each beat
74932.e: A trained heart has a larger stroke volume. So it needs fewer beats for the same amount of blood per minute.
74932.m: A trained heart beats more slowly at rest.

74933.q: What does the recovery heart rate, meaning how fast your pulse drops after exercise, show?
a: How well trained your endurance is
How fast you can do sums
74933.e: In well-trained people the pulse drops again faster after exercise. The recovery heart rate is therefore a sign of endurance fitness.
74933.m: A pulse that drops quickly after exercise shows good endurance.

74934.q: How long is one lap on the innermost lane of a normal athletics stadium?
74934.e: A standard running track measures 400 metres on the innermost lane. That is why the 400 metres goes exactly once around the stadium.
74934.m: One lap of the stadium is 400 metres long.

74935.q: How do you get the shot into the air in the shot put?
a: You push it forwards and upwards from your neck
You throw it with a straight arm like a ball
You hurl it on a wire
You roll it along the ground
74935.e: The shot rests against the neck and is pushed forwards and upwards with the arm. Throwing with an outstretched arm is not allowed.
74935.m: In the shot put the shot is pushed, not thrown.

74936.q: Which jumping event is made up of three parts: hop, step and jump?
74936.e: In the triple jump, after the run-up comes a hop onto the same leg, a step and the jump into the sandpit.
74936.m: The triple jump is made up of hop, step and jump.

74937.q: What is the high jump technique called in which you jump backwards over the bar?
74937.e: The American Dick Fosbury won Olympic gold with this technique in 1968. Today almost all high jumpers jump this way.
74937.m: In the Fosbury Flop you go over the bar on your back.

74938.q: How many hurdles are on the track in the 110 metres hurdles?
74938.e: In the men's 110 metres hurdles there are 10 hurdles to clear. In the women's 100 metres hurdles there are also 10 hurdles.
74938.m: In the sprint hurdles there are 10 hurdles.

74939.q: In which throwing event is the implement a ball on a steel wire with a handle?
74939.e: In the hammer throw the thrower spins several times in the circle and hurls the ball away on the wire. Because of the danger, there is a safety cage around the circle.
74939.m: The hammer is a ball on a wire with a handle.

74940.q: Which apparatus in Olympic artistic gymnastics is only used by men?
74940.e: Men compete on six pieces of apparatus, including the rings. Floor and vault are used by both, the balance beam only by women.
74940.m: The rings are a men's apparatus.

74941.q: On how many pieces of apparatus do women compete in Olympic artistic gymnastics?
74941.e: Women compete on vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor. Men compete on six pieces of apparatus.
74941.m: Female artistic gymnasts perform their routines on four pieces of apparatus.

74942.q: How wide is a balance beam in artistic gymnastics?
74942.e: The balance beam is only 10 centimetres wide and 5 metres long. Gymnasts perform jumps and turns on it.
74942.m: The balance beam is only 10 centimetres wide.

74943.q: What do you do with your head in a forward roll?
a: Tuck your chin to your chest
Turn your head to the side
74943.e: If you tuck your chin to your chest, your back becomes round and you roll over the back of your neck. This protects your head and neck.
74943.m: In a forward roll you tuck your chin to your chest.

74944.q: In which sport did Swiss athlete Giulia Steingruber win an Olympic medal in 2016?
74944.e: Giulia Steingruber won bronze on the vault in Rio in 2016. She is one of the most successful Swiss artistic gymnasts.
74944.m: Giulia Steingruber is a successful Swiss artistic gymnast.

74945.q: Swiss athlete Donghua Li became Olympic champion in 1996. In which sport?
74945.e: Donghua Li won gold on the pommel horse, a piece of gymnastics apparatus, in Atlanta in 1996. He had moved to Switzerland from China earlier.
74945.m: Donghua Li became Olympic champion in artistic gymnastics in 1996.

74946.q: Why do gymnasts rub their hands with chalk?
a: For dry hands and a better grip
74946.e: Gymnastics chalk is a white powder that absorbs sweat. With dry hands you are less likely to slip off the horizontal bar, parallel bars or rings.
74946.m: Chalk keeps hands dry and gives a good grip.

74947.q: Which swimming stroke comes first in the individual medley?
74947.e: In the individual medley the order is butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke and freestyle. So you start with butterfly.
74947.m: The individual medley starts with butterfly.

74948.q: Which swimming stroke comes first in the medley relay?
74948.e: In the medley relay the first swimmer swims backstroke, because it starts in the water. Then come breaststroke, butterfly and freestyle.
74948.m: The medley relay starts with backstroke.

74949.q: In which competitive swimming stroke do you start in the water instead of from the starting block?
74949.e: At the start, backstroke swimmers hold on to the starting block and push off from the wall in the water. All the others dive from the block.
74949.m: In backstroke you start in the water.

74950.q: In which swimming stroke do both legs move up and down at the same time like a dolphin's tail?
74950.e: In butterfly you do the dolphin kick. Both legs stay together and move in a wave together.
74950.m: In butterfly both legs kick at the same time.

74951.q: Which medal did Swiss swimmer Noè Ponti win in the 100 m butterfly in Tokyo in 2021?
74951.e: Noè Ponti from Ticino won bronze in the 100 m butterfly at the Olympic Games in Tokyo.
74951.m: Noè Ponti won Olympic bronze in Tokyo in 2021.

74953.q: How many players per team are on the full-size court in floorball, including the goalkeeper?
74953.e: On the full-size court each team has five outfield players and one goalkeeper. That makes six people.
74953.m: In full-size floorball, six players per team are on at the same time.

74954.q: What does the goalkeeper in floorball not have?
74954.e: The floorball goalkeeper plays without a stick. They block the ball with their body and may catch it with their hands in the goal area.
74954.m: Floorball goalkeepers play without a stick.

74955.q: How long does a floorball match on the full-size court last?
74955.e: A full-size match consists of three periods of 20 minutes each. There are breaks in between.
74955.m: Floorball is played in three periods of 20 minutes.

74956.q: How many holes does an official floorball ball have?
74956.e: The floorball ball is made of plastic, is hollow and has 26 holes. It is very light and can therefore go very fast.

74957.q: The Swiss call it “Unihockey”. What is this sport called internationally?
74957.e: Internationally, Unihockey is called floorball. The world governing body is called the International Floorball Federation.

74958.q: In which sport did the Swiss women become world champions for the first time in 2005?
74958.e: The Swiss women's floorball team won their first world title in Singapore in 2005.
74958.m: The Swiss women's floorball team became world champions in 2005.

74959.q: What are outfield players not allowed to do in floorball?
a: Play the ball with their head
Play the ball with their stick
Hold the stick with both hands
74959.e: In floorball the ball must not be played with the head. This protects against dangerous situations with sticks at head height.
74959.m: In floorball headers are not allowed.

74960.q: How many players per team are on the court in indoor volleyball?
74960.e: In indoor volleyball each team has six players. Three are at the front by the net, three at the back.
74960.m: In indoor volleyball there are six players per team.

74961.q: Up to how many points is a normal set played in indoor volleyball?
74961.e: A set goes up to 25 points, but you need at least a 2-point lead. A deciding set only goes up to 15.
74961.m: A volleyball set goes up to 25 points.

74962.q: What is the playing position called that only plays at the back and wears a shirt in a different colour?
74962.e: The libero is a defence specialist. They are not allowed to attack or block and stand out because of their different shirt colour.
74962.m: The libero is the defence specialist with a different shirt colour.

74963.q: What is playing the ball with both forearms held together called?
74963.e: For a dig you put your forearms together and let the ball bounce off them. This is mainly how you receive low and hard balls.
74963.m: In volleyball you receive low balls with a dig.

74964.q: How high is the volleyball net for men?
74964.e: For men, the top of the net is at 2.43 metres. For women it is 2.24 metres.
74964.m: The men's volleyball net is 2.43 metres high.

74965.q: How many people play in a beach volleyball team?
74965.e: Beach volleyball is played on sand with only two people per team. That is why each person has to master all the techniques.
74965.m: In beach volleyball two people make a team.

74966.q: How many players per team are on the court in indoor handball, including the goalkeeper?
74966.e: Each team has six outfield players and one goalkeeper. That makes seven people.
74966.m: In handball seven players per team are on at the same time.

74967.q: How long does a handball match last for adults?
74967.e: A handball match consists of two halves of 30 minutes each. There is a break in between.
74967.m: A handball match lasts two times 30 minutes.

74968.q: What is the longest you may hold the ball in your hand in handball?
74968.e: A player may hold the ball for no more than three seconds, even when standing still. This keeps the game fast.
74968.m: You may hold the handball for no more than three seconds.

74969.q: From what distance from the goal is a penalty throw taken in handball?
74969.e: That is why the penalty throw is also called a seven-metre throw. The thrower stands alone in front of the goalkeeper.
74969.m: The handball penalty throw is taken from seven metres.

74970.q: How far is the goal area line from the goal in handball?
74970.e: The goal area reaches 6 metres out in front of the goal. Apart from the goalkeeper, players are not allowed to enter it.
74970.m: The handball goal area reaches six metres in front of the goal.

74971.q: How long does a suspension last in handball?
74971.e: With a suspension, the player has to leave the court for 2 minutes. During this time their team plays with one player fewer.
74971.m: A suspension in handball lasts two minutes.

74972.q: What colours is a control flag in orienteering?
74972.e: A control flag is divided diagonally into orange and white. This makes it easy to see in the forest.
74972.m: Orienteering controls are orange and white.

74973.q: Which scale is typical for orienteering maps?
74973.e: Orienteering maps usually have a scale of 1:15,000 or 1:10,000. So at 1:15,000, one centimetre on the map equals 150 metres.
74973.m: Orienteering maps are very detailed large-scale maps.

74974.q: What does the colour yellow mean on an orienteering map?
74974.e: Yellow stands for open land such as meadows or fields. Water is blue, dense forest is green.
74974.m: On an orienteering map yellow means open land.

74975.q: What do brown contour lines that are very close together on an orienteering map show?
74975.e: Contour lines join points of the same height. If they are close together, the ground rises steeply over a short distance.
74975.m: Contour lines close together show steep ground.

74976.q: Which Swiss orienteer won 23 world championship gold medals?
74976.e: Simone Niggli-Luder from the canton of Bern won a total of 23 world titles. She is considered one of the best orienteers of all time.
74976.m: Simone Niggli is one of the most successful orienteers in the world.

74977.q: What does it mean to “set the map” (orient the map)?
a: Turn the map so that it matches the terrain
74977.e: When you set the map, you turn it so that its north matches north in the terrain. Then directions on the map match those in nature.
74977.m: A set map points the same way as the terrain.

74978.q: Who runs the Youth and Sport (J+S) programme in Switzerland?
74978.e: Youth and Sport is the federal government's sports promotion programme. It is led by the Federal Office of Sport (BASPO) and carried out together with the cantons.
74978.m: Youth and Sport is a federal programme.

74979.q: Who is the Youth and Sport programme meant for?
74979.e: Youth and Sport promotes sport for children and young people aged 5 to 20, for example in clubs and camps.
74979.m: Youth and Sport promotes sport for children and young people.

74980.q: What must leaders of J+S courses have?
74980.e: Anyone who leads J+S courses needs leader training in that sport. This ensures the quality of the courses.

74981.q: How does Youth and Sport support sports clubs and camps?
74981.e: The federal government pays contributions to J+S courses and camps, and it trains the leaders. This makes sports activities for children cheaper.
74981.m: Youth and Sport supports clubs with money and training.

74982.q: In which place in Ticino does BASPO run a well-known youth sports centre?
74982.e: The Centro Sportivo Nazionale della Gioventù in Tenero on Lake Maggiore belongs to BASPO. Many sports camps for young people take place there.
74982.m: There is a national youth sports centre in Tenero.

74983.q: Which federal department is also responsible for sport?
a: The Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport
The Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications
74983.e: The Federal Office of Sport (BASPO) belongs to the DDPS, the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport. The word sport is in the name.
74983.m: At federal level, sport belongs to the DDPS.

74984.q: What do Swiss wrestlers fight on?
74984.e: Swiss wrestling (Schwingen) takes place in a round ring filled with sawdust. The sawdust cushions the falls.
74984.m: Swiss wrestling takes place in sawdust.

74985.q: What is the winner of the Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival called?
74985.e: The winner of the Federal Festival may call himself Schwingerkönig, the Wrestling King. It is the highest title in Swiss wrestling.
74985.m: The winner of the Federal Festival is the Wrestling King.

74986.q: Which animal does the winner of the big Swiss wrestling festival get as a prize?
74986.e: At the Federal Wrestling Festival, animals are given as prizes. The Wrestling King receives a bull, called a “Muni” in Swiss German.
74986.m: The Wrestling King gets a bull.

74987.q: When is a Swiss wrestling bout won?
a: When both of the opponent's shoulder blades touch the ground
When the opponent leaves the sawdust
When the opponent lets go of the shorts
74987.e: A bout is won when the opponent lies in the sawdust with both shoulder blades at the same time. The winner must keep his grip on the shorts.
74987.m: You win by putting your opponent on both shoulder blades.

74988.q: What fabric are Swiss wrestling shorts made of?
74988.e: The short wrestling shorts are made of Zwilch, a very tear-resistant, coarse fabric. The wrestlers hold on to them.
74988.m: Swiss wrestling shorts are made of tough Zwilch.

74989.q: Who became Wrestling King in Pratteln in 2022?
74989.e: Joel Wicki from the Entlebuch won the Federal Festival in Pratteln in 2022. In 2019 Christian Stucki had won in Zug.
74989.m: Joel Wicki became Wrestling King in 2022.

74990.q: What does the winner traditionally do after a Swiss wrestling bout?
a: He brushes the sawdust off the loser's back
He shakes the sawdust over the audience
He takes off the wrestling shorts
74990.e: After the bout, the winner shakes the loser's hand and brushes the sawdust off his back. This shows respect and fairness.
74990.m: Fairness is part of the tradition in Swiss wrestling.

74991.q: How can you tell an easy endurance pace when jogging?
a: You can still have a conversation
You have to stop after a minute
You sprint as fast as possible
74991.e: At an easy base pace the body works aerobically. You breathe calmly enough to still speak in full sentences.
74991.m: At an easy endurance pace you can still chat.

74992.q: Which organ takes in oxygen from the air during sport?
74992.e: In the lungs, oxygen passes from the air you breathe into the blood. The blood then carries it to the muscles.
74992.m: The lungs take oxygen from the air.

74993.q: Besides carbohydrates, which energy source does the body use especially heavily during long, easy endurance exercise?
74993.e: During long efforts at a calm pace, the muscle burns a lot of fat with oxygen. Fat is a large energy store in the body.
74993.m: During long, easy exercise the body burns a lot of fat.

75037.q: Why shouldn't you put ice directly on the skin for a sports injury?
a: It can cause cold damage to the skin
75037.e: Direct contact with ice can cause local frostbite. That is why you put a cloth between the ice and the skin.
75037.m: Always put a cloth between the ice and your skin.

75038.q: Which emergency number do you call in Switzerland for an ambulance?
75038.e: 144 alerts the ambulance service. 117 is the police, 118 the fire brigade and 1414 Rega.
75038.m: In Switzerland you call an ambulance on 144.

75039.q: What is the emergency number of Rega, the Swiss air rescue service?
75039.e: Rega is alerted on 1414, for example for accidents in the mountains. From abroad you can reach it on +41 333 333 333.

75042.q: What is the right thing to do for a heavy nosebleed after being hit by a ball?
a: Lean your head forward and pinch the sides of your nose
75042.e: With your head forward, the blood flows out of your nose instead of into your throat. Cooling the back of your neck also helps.
75042.m: For a nosebleed, lean your head forward.

75094.q: Which family of instruments does the violin belong to?
75094.e: On a violin you draw a bow across the strings. That is why it belongs to the string instruments.
75094.m: The violin is a string instrument.

75095.q: Which family of instruments does the piano belong to?
75095.e: On a piano you press keys to play a note. That is why it counts as a keyboard instrument.
75095.m: The piano is a keyboard instrument.

75096.q: Which family of instruments does the guitar belong to?
75096.e: The strings of a guitar are plucked with the fingers. That is why it is a plucked instrument.
75096.m: The guitar is a plucked instrument.

75097.q: Which family of instruments does the clarinet belong to?
75097.e: The clarinet is made of wood and has a reed on the mouthpiece. It belongs to the woodwind instruments.
75097.m: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument.

75098.q: The saxophone is made of metal. Which family does it still belong to?
75098.e: The saxophone has a reed, like the clarinet. That is why it counts as a woodwind instrument.
75098.m: Because of its reed, the saxophone is a woodwind instrument.

75099.q: Which family of instruments does the xylophone belong to?
75099.e: On a xylophone you strike wooden bars with beaters. That is why it belongs to the percussion instruments.
75099.m: The xylophone is a percussion instrument with wooden bars.

75100.q: Which family of instruments does the French horn belong to?
75100.e: The French horn is made of brass, and the sound is made by the lips on the mouthpiece. It is a brass instrument.
75100.m: The French horn is a brass instrument.

75101.q: Which instrument is a percussion instrument?
75101.e: The triangle is a bent metal bar that you strike with a small rod. That is why it is a percussion instrument.
75101.m: The triangle is a small metal percussion instrument.

75102.q: Which large keyboard instrument in church has lots of pipes?
75102.e: On an organ, air flows through pipes when you press the keys. You often find one in churches.
75102.m: The organ is a keyboard instrument with many pipes.

75103.q: What is volume called in music?
75103.e: In music, dynamics means how loudly or quietly something is played.
75103.m: Volume in music is called dynamics.

75104.e: Decrescendo comes from Italian and means decreasing. So the music gets quieter bit by bit.
75104.m: In a decrescendo the music gradually gets quieter.

75105.q: What does the sign “ff” mean in written music?
75105.e: The abbreviation ff stands for fortissimo. That means you play very loudly.
75105.m: The sign ff means you play very loudly.

75106.q: What does the sign “mf” mean in written music?
75106.e: The abbreviation mf stands for mezzo forte. Mezzo means half, so you play moderately loudly.
75106.m: The sign mf means moderately loud.

75107.q: Why was the piano once called the “pianoforte”?
a: It can play quietly and loudly
75107.e: Piano means quiet and forte means loud. On a pianoforte the volume depends on how hard you strike the key.
75107.m: The pianoforte can play quietly and loudly.

75108.q: What do you put into a trumpet to make it sound quieter?
75108.e: A mute is put into the bell at the front. It makes the sound quieter and changes it.
75108.m: A mute makes a trumpet quieter.

75109.q: How do you play a quiet note on a drum?
75109.e: The more gently you hit the skin, the less it vibrates. That is why the note sounds quieter.
75109.m: Hitting a drum gently plays it quietly.

75110.q: Which word describes how high or low a note is?
75110.e: Pitch tells you whether a note sounds high or low.
75110.m: Whether a note is high or low is called its pitch.

75111.e: Large bells vibrate more slowly than small ones. That is why they sound lower.
75111.m: Large bells sound lower than small ones.

75112.q: Which bars on a xylophone sound higher?
75112.e: Short bars vibrate faster than long ones. That is why they sound higher.
75112.m: On a xylophone the short bars sound higher.

75113.q: Which pipes of a panpipe sound lowest?
75113.e: More air vibrates in a long pipe. That is why the note sounds lower.
75113.m: On a panpipe the long pipes sound low.

75114.q: What happens to the note of a guitar string when you tighten it?
75114.e: A tightly stretched string vibrates faster. That is why it sounds higher.
75114.m: The tighter a string is, the higher it sounds.

75115.e: The bassoon has a very long, folded tube. That is why it sounds low.
75115.m: The bassoon is a low woodwind instrument.

75116.q: Which animal has a very high voice?
75116.e: The mouse is small and squeaks in a high voice. Big animals like bears, cows and lions growl, moo or roar deeply.
75116.m: The little mouse squeaks in a high voice.

75117.e: Small birds chirp with bright, high notes. Thunder, engines and large bells sound low.

75118.e: Allegro is Italian and means cheerful. In music it means a fast, lively tempo.

75119.e: Adagio is Italian and means at ease. So you play slowly.

75120.e: Presto means quick in Italian. In music it is one of the fastest tempos.

75121.e: Accelerando means speeding up. The tempo gets faster bit by bit.
75121.m: In an accelerando the music gradually gets faster.

75122.e: Ritardando means holding back. The tempo gets slower bit by bit, often at the end of a piece.
75122.m: In a ritardando the music gradually gets slower.

75123.e: Andante comes from the Italian word for walking. The tempo is calm, like a gentle stroll.
75123.m: Andante means a calm, walking tempo.

75124.q: What does the number 120 on a metronome show?
75124.e: A metronome counts beats per minute. At 120 it ticks once every half second.
75124.m: The number on a metronome shows the beats per minute.

75125.q: Which famous, very fast piece of music imitates a flying insect?
75125.e: “Flight of the Bumblebee” is by the Russian composer Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov. The fast notes sound like the buzzing of a bumblebee.
75125.m: Flight of the Bumblebee is a very fast piece of music.

75126.q: How many beats does a minim (half note) last in 4/4 time?
75126.e: A semibreve (whole note) lasts 4 beats. The minim lasts half as long, so 2 beats.

75127.q: How many crotchets (quarter notes) last as long as a minim (half note)?
75127.e: A crotchet lasts 1 beat, a minim 2 beats. So you need 2 crotchets.
75127.m: Two crotchets last as long as a minim.

75128.q: What does a crotchet (quarter note) look like?
75128.e: The crotchet has a filled-in black note head and a stem without a tail.
75128.m: The crotchet has a black head and a stem.

75129.q: What does a minim (half note) look like?
75129.e: The minim has an empty white note head and a stem.
75129.m: The minim has a white head and a stem.

75130.q: Which note has a white head and no stem?
75130.e: The semibreve is just an empty oval head without a stem.

75131.q: Which note has a small tail on its stem?
75131.e: The quaver looks like a crotchet with a tail. Two quavers are often joined with a beam.
75131.m: You can recognise a quaver by its tail.

75132.q: What is the rest called that lasts as long as a minim (half note)?
75132.e: Every note has a matching rest of the same length. So the minim rest lasts two beats and looks like a little hat sitting on the line.
75132.m: The minim rest lasts as long as a minim.

75133.q: How long does a crotchet (quarter) rest last?
75133.e: A crotchet rest lasts exactly as long as a crotchet, so one beat.
75133.m: A crotchet rest lasts one beat.

a: At the start of the stave
At the end of the stave
75134.e: The clef is right at the front of every stave. It shows which note sits on which line.
75134.m: The clef is at the start of every stave.

75135.q: Which clef is used for low notes?
75135.e: The bass clef is used for low instruments such as the cello, the tuba or the left hand on the piano.
75135.m: The bass clef is used for low notes.

75136.q: What are the short lines above or below the five lines of the stave called?
75136.e: For very high or very low notes you draw short ledger lines above or below the stave.
75136.m: Ledger lines help with very high and very low notes.

75137.e: A note head can sit on a line or in the space between two lines. That gives more room for different notes.
75137.m: Notes sit on the lines or in the spaces.

75138.q: How many spaces are there between the five lines of the stave?
75138.e: Between five lines there is always one space fewer than lines, so 4 spaces.
75138.m: There are four spaces between the five lines of the stave.

75139.q: Which line of the stave counts as the first line?
75139.e: The lines of the stave are counted from the bottom up. So the bottom line is the first.
75139.m: The lines of the stave are counted from the bottom up.

75140.q: In the treble clef, which note sits on the first ledger line below the five lines?
75140.e: In the treble clef, C sits on a small ledger line below the stave. The C major scale often starts on it.
75140.m: The low C in the treble clef sits on a ledger line.

75141.q: What is the double line at the very end of a piece of music called?
75141.e: A final double bar line is made of one thin and one thick line. It shows the end of the piece.
75141.m: The final double bar line shows the end of a piece of music.

75142.q: Which animal appears in the song “Det äne am Bergli”?
75142.e: In this Swiss folk song a white goat stands over on the hill. The farmer wants to milk it.
75142.m: The song “Det äne am Bergli” is about a white goat.

75143.q: What does the goat in the song “Det äne am Bergli” do when the farmer wants to milk it?
75143.e: When the farmer wants to milk the white goat, it kicks him. That is what this funny Swiss folk song tells.
75143.m: In the song the white goat kicks the farmer.

75144.q: What weather does the song “Es schneielet, es beielet” tell of?
75144.e: This Swiss German song describes a snowstorm in winter. “Schneielet” means that it is snowing in Swiss German.
75144.m: The song “Es schneielet, es beielet” is a winter song.
