75572.m: A bust portrait shows the person down to the chest.

75574.q: Which city full of canals did the Italian painter Canaletto paint especially often?
75574.e: In the 18th century, Canaletto painted very precise views of Venice. Pictures like these are called vedute.
75574.m: Canaletto painted precise views of Venice.

75575.q: Why do artists often paint tiny people next to the mountains in a picture of the Alps?
a: To make the mountains look enormous
To make the picture more colourful
To make the sky look brighter
75575.e: Next to small figures, you can see how huge glaciers and rocks are. The Aargau painter Caspar Wolf already used this trick in the 18th century.
75575.m: Small people make mountains look huge in a picture.

75576.q: Harald Naegeli became known in the late 1970s as the “Sprayer of Zurich”. What did he spray on house walls at night?
75576.e: Harald Naegeli sprayed delicate stick figures on walls in Zurich at night. He was convicted for it, but later also honoured as an artist.
75576.m: Harald Naegeli is known as the “Sprayer of Zurich”.

75577.q: What do you call the quickly sprayed signature or name abbreviation of a graffiti artist?
75577.e: A tag is a sprayer's personal signature. It is the simplest form of graffiti.
75577.m: A tag is a sprayer's signature.

75578.q: What do you call a large wall painting on the front of a building, often painted legally?
75578.e: The word mural comes from the Latin “murus” for wall. Murals often cover whole walls and are usually commissioned.
75578.m: A mural is a large wall painting.

75579.q: What is the street art form called where trees or railings are wrapped in knitting?
75579.e: In yarn bombing, also called urban knitting, objects in public spaces are covered with knitted wool. It can easily be removed again.
75579.m: In yarn bombing, the city is decorated with wool.

75580.q: What are posters or paper pictures called that are stuck onto walls with paste?
75580.e: Paste-ups are painted or printed at home and then stuck to the wall with paste. This way even large pictures can be put up quickly.
75580.m: Paste-ups are paper pictures stuck onto walls.

75581.q: Which New York artist drew figures in chalk on empty advertising spaces in the subway in the 1980s?
75581.e: Keith Haring drew with white chalk on black, empty poster spaces in the New York subway. His simple, lively figures became world-famous.
75581.m: Keith Haring drew chalk figures in the subway.

75582.q: What is the technique called where a picture is created by cleaning dirt off a wall?
75582.e: In reverse graffiti, nothing is sprayed on; instead, dirt is removed in a planned way. The picture is formed by the clean areas.
75582.m: Reverse graffiti is made by cleaning off dirt.

75583.q: What did Paul Klee discover for his art on his trip to Tunisia in 1914?
75583.e: The bright light in North Africa made a deep impression on Klee. He wrote in his diary that he and colour were now one.
75583.m: On his trip to Tunisia, Klee discovered colour.

75584.q: Which musical instrument did Paul Klee play very well?
75584.e: Paul Klee came from a family of musicians and was an excellent violinist. Music also influenced his pictures.
75584.m: Paul Klee was also a good violinist.

75585.q: What shape are the roofs of the Zentrum Paul Klee in Bern?
75585.e: The Zentrum Paul Klee opened in 2005. Its three wave-shaped roofs are reminiscent of a hilly landscape.
75585.m: The Zentrum Paul Klee has three wave-shaped roofs.

75586.q: Apart from people, what did the Swiss painter Ferdinand Hodler especially like to paint?
75586.e: Hodler often painted Swiss landscapes such as Lake Thun or the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. Clear shapes and calm colours are typical.
75586.m: Ferdinand Hodler liked to paint mountains and lakes.

75587.q: What do Ferdinand Hodler's large murals in the Swiss National Museum in Zurich show?
75587.e: For the National Museum, Hodler painted the retreat of the Confederates from the Battle of Marignano in 1515. At the time the pictures caused heated debate.
75587.m: Hodler's murals in the National Museum show a battle of the Confederates.

75588.q: Which Swiss lake did Ferdinand Hodler paint especially often with the mountains in the background?
75588.e: Hodler painted Lake Thun with the Stockhorn range in many versions. He emphasised clear, horizontal bands of shore, water and mountains.

75589.q: What do you call art like Jean Tinguely's machines, where the work moves?
75589.e: The word kinetic comes from the Greek word for movement. Tinguely's sculptures made of scrap turn, clatter and rattle.
75589.m: Kinetic art is art in motion.

75590.q: What material did Jean Tinguely often use to build his machine sculptures?
75590.e: Tinguely collected wheels, iron parts and motors. From these he built sculptures that turn, clatter and rattle.
75590.m: Tinguely built his machines from scrap.

75591.q: On which river is the Museum Tinguely in Basel?
75591.e: The Museum Tinguely opened on the bank of the Rhine in Basel in 1996. It shows the largest collection of Tinguely's works.
75591.m: The Museum Tinguely is on the Rhine in Basel.

75692.q: What can you count on the cross-section of a tree trunk to estimate its age?
75692.e: A tree usually grows a new ring every year. If you count the growth rings, you know roughly how old the tree is.
75692.m: Each growth ring stands for about one year.

75693.q: What do you call a flat, long piece of wood that you can use to build a shelf, for example?
75693.e: Flat, long planks are sawn from a tree trunk. They are used to build shelves, boxes or floors.
75693.m: A plank is a flat piece of wood.

75694.q: What happens to wood when it falls into water?
75694.e: Most kinds of wood are lighter than water, so they float on top. That is why rafts and boats used to be made of wood.
75694.m: Most kinds of wood float on water.

75695.q: What do you use to make a rough wooden edge smooth?
75695.e: Sandpaper is coated with fine, hard grains. If you rub it over the wood, the surface becomes smooth.

75696.q: What is a small, sharp piece of wood called that can stick into your skin?
75696.e: A splinter is a thin sliver of wood that can dig into your skin. That is why wooden edges are sanded smooth.
75696.m: A splinter is a small sliver of wood.

75697.q: What is the outer protective layer of a tree trunk?
75697.e: Bark wraps around the trunk like a skin. It protects the tree from cold, animals and diseases.

75698.q: What is the dark, round spot in a plank called, where a branch once grew out of the trunk?
75698.e: Where a branch grew out of the trunk, you can see a round, often dark spot in the plank. This spot is called a knot.
75698.m: A knot in a plank shows where a branch once grew.

75699.q: What do you call the lines in the wood that you can see on a plank?
75699.e: The grain comes from the growth rings and the wood fibres. That is why every plank has its own pattern.
75699.m: The grain is the natural pattern in wood.

75700.q: What is paper mostly made from today?
75700.e: To make paper, wood fibres are mixed with lots of water into a pulp. Thin sheets are then pressed and dried from it.
75700.m: Paper is mostly made from wood fibres.

75701.e: Waste paper is paper that has already been used. You bundle it up and hand it in for collection so that new paper can be made from it.
75701.m: New paper can be made from waste paper.

75702.q: What is the Japanese art of folding figures out of paper called?
75702.e: Origami comes from Japan and means paper folding. You fold animals, flowers or boats without scissors or glue.
75702.m: Origami is the art of paper folding.

75703.q: What happens to paper when it gets wet?
a: It goes soft and tears easily
75703.e: Water gets in between the fibres of the paper. As a result the fibres hold together less well and the paper tears easily.

75704.q: What do you call paper that is dyed and used for craft work?
75704.e: Coloured paper comes in many colours. You cut and glue it for pictures, cards and decorations.
75704.m: Coloured paper comes in many colours for crafts.

75705.q: What is the craft material made of soaked paper and glue that becomes hard when it dries?
75705.e: For papier-mâché, you stick strips of paper in layers onto a shape, for example a balloon. When it dries, everything becomes firm.
75705.m: You can make papier-mâché from paper and glue.

75706.q: Which paper is see-through enough to trace a picture underneath?
75706.e: Tracing paper lets a lot of light through. That is why you can see a picture underneath and draw over it with a pencil.
75706.m: You can trace pictures with tracing paper.

75707.q: What is cardboard like compared with normal paper?
75707.e: Like paper, cardboard is made of fibres, but it is much thicker. That is why it is stiff and good for boxes.
75707.m: Cardboard is thicker and firmer than paper.

75708.q: What is cardboard with a wavy layer in the middle called?
75708.e: Corrugated cardboard has a wavy paper layer inside between two smooth layers. This makes it light but still strong.
75708.m: Corrugated cardboard has a wavy layer inside.

75709.q: What is often made from corrugated cardboard?
75709.e: Corrugated cardboard is light and strong. That is why it is used for boxes for parcels and for moving house.
75709.m: Boxes for parcels are often made of corrugated cardboard.

75710.q: What helps cardboard fold nice and straight?
75710.e: If you score the fold line along a ruler with a bone folder or a blunt point, the cardboard bends exactly there. This makes the edge nice and straight.
75710.m: A scored line makes folding cardboard easier.

a: Soft earth that you can shape
75711.e: Clay is a fine earth from nature. With water it becomes soft and you can knead and shape it.
75711.m: Clay is an earth you can shape.

75712.q: What do you have to do with a clay figure to make it really hard?
75712.e: Dried clay breaks easily and goes soft again in water. Only at very high heat, much hotter than in a kitchen, does it become hard as stone.
75712.m: Clay only becomes really hard when it is fired.

75713.q: What is the special oven called in which clay is fired?
75713.e: A kiln gets much hotter than a kitchen oven. This great heat makes the clay hard.
75713.m: Clay is fired in a kiln.

75714.q: What happens to clay if it is left in the air for a long time?
a: It always stays just as soft
75714.e: Clay contains water. In the air the water evaporates and the clay becomes dry and firm. That is why clay is covered with a damp cloth or plastic.
75714.m: Clay dries out in the air.

75715.q: What do you call a thick roll of clay used to build up a pot layer by layer?
75715.e: In the coil technique, you roll clay into long sausages. You lay them in rings on top of each other and smooth them together well.
75715.m: You can build pots with clay coils.

75716.q: On which spinning disc do you shape bowls out of clay?
75716.e: On the potter's wheel, the clay spins quickly round and round. With wet hands you shape it into round pots.
75716.m: On a potter's wheel, the clay spins round.

75717.q: What is the shiny, glass-like coating on clay crockery called?
75717.e: The glaze is applied before the second firing. In the heat it melts into a smooth, often coloured layer.

75718.q: What do you call someone who makes pots and bowls out of clay?
75718.e: Potters shape pots, plates and cups out of clay. Today the job is often called ceramicist.
75718.m: A potter makes pots out of clay.

75719.q: Which animal does most wool come from?
75719.e: Sheep have a thick, curly coat. It is sheared off and made into wool.

75720.q: How do you make a long thread from loose wool?
75720.e: When spinning, the wool fibres are pulled and twisted. This creates a strong, long thread.

75721.q: What is a wound-up piece of wool thread called?
75721.e: Wool is often bought as a ball. The thread is wound up in a round shape and is easy to unwind.
75721.m: A ball of wool is wool that has been wound up.

75722.q: Which tool with a small hook at the tip do you need for crocheting?
75722.e: The crochet hook has a small hook at the front. You use it to pull the wool through loops and crochet a pot holder, for example.
75722.m: You need a crochet hook to crochet.

75723.q: What is a single loop in knitting called?
75723.e: A piece of knitting is made of many stitches. Each stitch is a small loop of yarn.
75723.m: Knitting is made of many stitches.

75724.q: What do you get if you rub wool with warm soapy water?
75724.e: Warmth, soap and rubbing make the wool fibres hook firmly into each other. This creates a dense fabric called felt.
75724.m: Wool, soapy water and rubbing make felt.

75725.q: What are woollen clothes especially good for?
75725.e: Lots of air is trapped between the crinkly wool fibres. This air holds in your body heat.
75725.m: Wool keeps you nice and warm.

75726.q: Where do the soft fibres of cotton grow?
a: In the seed pods of a plant
75726.e: The cotton plant forms pods with white, fluffy fibres. These fibres are spun into yarn for fabrics.
75726.m: Cotton comes from the cotton plant.

75727.q: Which animal makes the threads for silk?
75727.e: The caterpillar of the silk moth spins itself into a cocoon made of one long, fine thread. Silk is made from these threads.

75728.q: Which plant is linen made from?
75728.e: Flax has long fibres in its stem. These are woven into the cool fabric linen.

a: A template for cutting out fabric
75729.e: A sewing pattern shows the shape of the fabric pieces. You lay it on the fabric, trace round it and cut out the pieces.
75729.m: A sewing pattern helps you cut out fabric.

75730.q: Which side of the fabric do you see when you wear a piece of clothing normally?
75730.e: On fabric, the nice outer side is called the right side. The inner side is called the wrong side.
75730.m: The nice side of a fabric is called the right side.

75731.q: What often happens to a woollen jumper if you wash it too hot?
75731.e: Heat and movement make the wool fibres felt together. The jumper contracts and gets smaller.
75731.m: Wool can shrink in a hot wash.

75732.q: What is a small piece of fabric called that you sew over a hole in your trousers?
75732.e: You cover a hole with a patch. You sew it on or iron it on, so you can keep wearing the trousers.
75732.m: You mend a hole with a patch.

75733.q: How do you carry scissors safely?
75733.e: You hold the scissors closed with the point facing down. That way you will not hurt anyone if you trip.
75733.m: Carry scissors closed with the point down.

75734.q: How do you pass scissors to someone correctly?
75734.e: You hold the scissors by the closed blades and offer the other person the handle. That way nobody can cut themselves.

75735.q: How many blades does a normal pair of scissors have?
75735.e: Scissors have two blades that slide past each other. The paper or fabric is cut between them.

75736.q: Why shouldn't you cut paper with fabric scissors?
75736.e: Paper contains tiny hard particles that wear down the sharp blades. Blunt fabric scissors no longer cut fabric cleanly.
75736.m: Only cut fabric with fabric scissors.

75737.q: What helps when cutting a curve with scissors?
75737.e: For a curve, the scissors stay still and you turn the paper with your other hand. This makes the line nice and round.
75737.m: For curves, turn the paper, not the scissors.

75738.q: Which scissors cut a zigzag edge into fabric?
75738.e: Pinking shears have jagged blades. The zigzag edge stops the fabric fraying so quickly at the edge.
75738.m: Pinking shears cut a zigzag edge.

75739.q: Which scissors with rounded tips are meant for children doing crafts?
75739.e: Craft scissors have rounded tips. That way you are less likely to prick yourself when cutting paper.
75739.m: Children cut paper with craft scissors.

75740.q: Which glue is good for sticking wood?
75740.e: PVA glue is white but turns clear as it dries. It sticks pieces of wood together very firmly.
75740.m: Wood sticks well with PVA glue.

75741.q: What must you do after joining two pieces of wood with glue?
a: Press them firmly and let them dry
Paint them while the glue is wet
75741.e: Glue needs time to dry. If you press the pieces firmly together and leave them alone, the joint holds better.
75741.m: Glued pieces must be pressed together and left to dry.

75742.q: Which glue comes in a small stick that you twist up like a lipstick?
75742.e: You twist the glue stick up and rub it over the paper. It is clean and good for paper crafts.
75742.m: A glue stick is good for paper.

75743.q: What is a glue called that you can mix from flour and water?
75743.e: Flour and water together make a sticky mixture. This paste is used for paper crafts or wallpaper, for example.
75743.m: You can make paste from flour and water.

75744.q: What is especially dangerous about a hot glue gun?
75744.e: A glue stick is melted inside the hot glue gun. The liquid glue is so hot that you can burn yourself on it.
75744.m: Hot glue can burn your skin.

75745.q: Why should you only put on a little glue?
a: Too much glue oozes out and dries slowly
Too much glue turns the wood red
Too much glue makes the wood melt
Too much glue makes the wood lighter
75745.e: A thin layer of glue is enough. Too much glue oozes out at the edges, leaves marks and takes longer to dry.
75745.m: A thin layer of glue is enough.

a: A strip with a sticky side
75746.e: Sticky tape is a thin strip coated with glue on one side. You can tear it off and stick it on straight away.
75746.m: Sticky tape is sticky on one side.

75747.q: What does a saw have so that it can cut wood?
75747.e: The saw blade has lots of small, sharp teeth. As it moves back and forth, they remove the wood bit by bit.
75747.m: A saw cuts with its teeth.

75748.q: What is the fine wood powder called that is made when sawing?
75748.e: The teeth of the saw tear out tiny bits of wood. These fall down as fine sawdust.

75749.q: What do you use to hold the wood firmly while sawing?
75749.e: The wood must be held tightly while sawing, for example with a clamp or in a vice. Otherwise it slips and you can hurt yourself.
75749.m: When sawing, the wood must be clamped tight.

75750.q: Which saw can you use to cut fine curves out of thin wood?
75750.e: A fretsaw has a very thin blade. You can use it to cut curves and shapes out of thin plywood.
75750.m: You cut fine curves with a fretsaw.

75752.q: Why should you wear safety goggles when sawing?
a: So that no bits of wood fly into your eyes
So that the wood looks nicer
So that the saw is quieter
75752.e: When sawing, small bits of wood can fly around. Safety goggles protect your eyes from them.
75752.m: Safety goggles protect your eyes in the workshop.

75753.q: What do you draw on the wood before you saw?
75753.e: With a pencil and ruler you mark exactly where to saw. This makes the cut straight and in the right place.
75753.m: Before sawing, you mark the line.

75754.q: What do you usually need a hammer for?
75754.e: You use a hammer to knock nails into wood. While doing so, you take good care of your fingers.
75754.m: You knock in nails with a hammer.

75755.q: What are the two main parts of a hammer?
75755.e: A hammer has a heavy metal head and a handle to hold it by. The handle is often made of wood.
75755.m: A hammer has a head and a handle.

75756.q: What is the split, curved part of a claw hammer for?
75756.e: On a claw hammer, one side of the head is split. You can use it to grip a bent nail and pull it out.
75756.m: You pull out nails with the claw.

75757.q: Which hammer has a head made of rubber or wood so that it does not scratch anything?
75757.e: A soft hammer made of wood or rubber knocks parts together without making dents. You need it, for example, when fitting wooden parts together.
75757.m: A rubber mallet leaves no dents.

75758.q: What are nails usually made of?
75758.e: Nails are usually made of steel, which is a metal. That is why they are hard enough to go into wood.
75758.m: Nails are usually made of metal.

75759.q: What is the wide, flat end of a nail that you hit called?
75759.e: A nail has a flat head at the top and a point at the bottom. You hit the head with the hammer.
75759.m: You hit the head of the nail with the hammer.

75760.q: How do you start knocking in a nail?
a: Hold the nail with two fingers and tap lightly
Hold the nail with two fingers and hit hard straight away
Let go of the nail and hit hard straight away
Hold the nail in your fist and hit hard
75760.e: At first you hold the nail between your thumb and index finger and tap very lightly. As soon as it is firmly in, you take your fingers away and hit harder.
75760.m: First tap lightly, then hit harder.

75761.q: What often happens if you knock a nail in too close to the edge of a plank?
75761.e: The nail pushes the wood fibres apart. If there is too little wood at the edge, the plank splits.
75761.m: Do not knock nails in too close to the edge.

75762.q: What is the small hole in a sewing needle called, through which you thread the cotton?
75762.e: A sewing needle has a point at one end and a small hole at the other. This hole is called the eye.
75762.m: The thread goes through the eye of the needle.

75763.q: What protects your finger from the needle when sewing by hand?
75763.e: You put the thimble on your middle finger. With it you can push the needle through the fabric without pricking yourself.
75763.m: A thimble protects your finger when sewing.

75764.q: What do you put at the end of the thread so that it does not slip through the fabric?
75764.e: A knot at the end of the thread is thicker than the hole in the fabric. That way the thread stays caught at the first stitch.
75764.m: A knot holds the thread in the fabric.

75765.q: What is the line called where two pieces of fabric are sewn together?
75765.e: Where two pieces of fabric are joined with stitches, a seam is formed. On clothes you can see seams at the sides, for example.
75765.m: A seam joins two pieces of fabric.

75766.q: What is the simple stitch called where the needle keeps going up and down through the fabric?
75766.e: With running stitch, you stitch up and down at equal distances. This makes a dashed line.
75766.m: Running stitch is a simple up-and-down stitch.

75767.q: In which stitch do two slanting stitches together form an X?
75767.e: In cross stitch, you first sew a slanting stitch and then cross it with a second one. This way pictures are made from lots of little Xs.

75768.q: Which machine lets you sew faster than by hand?
75768.e: A sewing machine moves the needle up and down very fast. This makes long, even seams in a short time.

75769.q: What do you use to fix pieces of fabric together before sewing?
75769.e: Pins often have a small head. You use them to hold the pieces of fabric in place so that they do not slip while sewing.
75769.m: Pins hold fabric together before sewing.

75770.q: What do you need buttons on clothes for?
75770.e: A button is pushed through a small slit in the fabric. This keeps a shirt or jacket closed, for example.

75771.q: What is the slit in the fabric that you push the button through called?
75771.e: A buttonhole is a narrow slit with a sewn edge. The button fits exactly through it.
75771.m: The button goes in the buttonhole.

75772.q: How many holes do many flat buttons have?
75772.e: Many flat buttons have two or four holes. You sew the button onto the fabric through these holes.
75772.m: Many buttons have two or four holes.

75773.q: What do you need to sew a button back on?
75773.e: You thread a needle and sew through the holes of the button into the fabric. At the end you fasten off the thread well.
75773.m: You sew on a button with needle and thread.

75774.q: What is a button called that has two parts and is pressed shut with a click?
75774.e: A press stud has a top part and a bottom part. When you press them together, they snap into place with a click.
75774.m: A press stud closes with a click.

75775.q: What can buttons be made of, for example?
75775.e: Buttons come in many materials. They are often made of plastic, metal, wood or horn.

75776.q: Which fastening is often used on jackets instead of buttons and has lots of little teeth?
75776.e: In a zip, lots of little teeth lock into each other. You open and close it quickly with the slider.
75776.m: A zip has lots of little teeth.

75777.q: How many strands do you use to make a simple plait?
75777.e: For a simple plait, you divide hair or threads into three strands. Then you take turns laying the left and the right strand over the middle one.
75777.m: A simple plait has three strands.

75778.q: Which Swiss Sunday bread is plaited from strands of dough?
75778.e: In Switzerland, people often eat butter Zopf for breakfast on Sundays. The dough is plaited before baking.
75778.m: The Sunday Zopf is plaited from dough.

75779.q: What material are baskets often woven from?
75779.e: Willow rods are long and bendy. That is why they are easy to weave into strong baskets.
75779.m: Baskets are often woven from willow rods.

75780.q: What do you do with the strands when plaiting?
a: You lay them over each other in turn
75780.e: When plaiting, you cross several strands over each other in turn. This way they hold together without glue.
75780.m: When plaiting, the strands cross over each other in turn.

75781.q: What can you weave from strips of paper?
75781.e: You cut paper into strips and weave them over and under each other. This makes a colourful paper mat.
75781.m: You can weave a mat from paper strips.

75782.q: Which device is used to weave fabric?
75782.e: Lots of threads are stretched on a loom. You pass a crosswise thread over and under them again and again.
75782.m: Fabric is woven on a loom.

75783.q: What are the threads stretched lengthways in weaving called?
75783.e: The warp threads are first stretched tightly lengthways. The crosswise thread that is passed through them is called the weft.
75783.m: In weaving, the warp threads run lengthways.

75784.q: What do you need the weaving comb for when weaving?
a: To push the crosswise threads tightly together
75784.e: After each row, you press the new crosswise thread against the previous rows with the weaving comb. This makes the fabric dense and firm.
75784.m: The weaving comb pushes the rows tightly together.

75785.q: What is the firm edge at the side of a woven fabric that does not fray called?
75785.e: At the side, the crosswise thread turns and runs back. This creates a firm edge, the selvedge, which does not fray.
75785.m: The selvedge is the firm edge of a woven fabric.

75786.q: What do you use to pass the thread through when weaving on a small weaving frame?
a: A weaving needle or a shuttle
75786.e: The crosswise thread is wound onto a shuttle or threaded into a large weaving needle. This lets you pass it easily through the stretched threads.
75786.m: The shuttle carries the thread when weaving.

75787.q: What can you weave on a small weaving frame at school?
75787.e: A small weaving frame produces a small, flat piece of fabric. You can make it into a coaster or a doll's rug, for example.
75787.m: A weaving frame makes a small piece of fabric.

75788.q: Which part of the cotton plant are cotton fibres obtained from?
75788.e: Cotton fibres grow as fine hairs on the seeds inside the seed pod. When the pod bursts open, the white fibre puffs out.
75788.m: Cotton is made of the seed hairs of the cotton plant.

75789.q: Why are towels often made of cotton?
a: It soaks up a lot of water.
It builds up a lot of static.
75789.e: Cotton is very absorbent and can take up a lot of moisture. That is why cotton towels dry you well.
75789.m: Cotton is absorbent, so it is good for towels.

75790.q: Which protein is the main component of sheep's wool?
75790.e: Wool is animal hair and, like our hair and nails, is made mainly of the protein keratin.
75790.m: Sheep's wool is made mainly of the protein keratin.

75791.q: Why can a woollen jumper felt in water that is too hot with lots of rubbing?
a: The fibres have scales that hook together.
75791.e: Wool hairs have a layer of scales. With warmth, moisture and movement, the scales hook together and the fabric becomes dense and smaller.
75791.m: Wool felts because the scales of the hairs hook into each other.

75792.q: Which leaves does the silkworm caterpillar feed on?
75792.e: The caterpillar of the silk moth eats the leaves of the mulberry tree. Then it spins itself into a cocoon made of one long silk thread.

75793.q: Which natural fibre is a very long continuous thread (filament)?
75793.e: The silkworm's cocoon is made of a single thread several hundred metres long. Other natural fibres are short fibres that have to be spun into yarn.
75793.m: Silk is the only natural fibre that comes as a continuous thread.

75794.q: Which plant is the fibre for linen obtained from?
75794.e: Linen is made from the stem fibres of flax. Linen fabrics are strong and feel cool.

75795.q: What raw material is polyester mainly made from?
75795.e: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made of plastic. The plastic is usually made from crude oil.
75795.m: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made from crude oil.

75796.q: What happens to a polyester fibre in a burn test?
a: It melts into a hard bead.
It burns to soft, grey ash.
It does not burn at all.
75796.e: Polyester is a plastic and melts in the flame. Afterwards a hard ball is left that you cannot crush.
75796.m: Synthetic fibres melt into hard beads in a burn test.

75797.q: In weaving, what is the opening between the raised and the lowered warp threads called?
75797.e: Raising some of the warp threads creates a gap. The crosswise thread is passed through this shed.
75797.m: In weaving, the crosswise thread runs through the shed.

75798.q: What is the thread called that is passed crosswise through the stretched threads in weaving?
75798.e: The weft thread is shot crosswise between the lengthways threads. Together the two sets of threads form the fabric.
75798.m: The crosswise thread in weaving is called the weft.

75799.q: Which tool is used to pass the crosswise thread through the warp on a loom?
75799.e: The shuttle carries a small bobbin with the thread. It is pushed from one side to the other through the opened warp threads.
75799.m: The shuttle carries the crosswise thread through the warp.

75800.q: Which part of the loom presses the new crosswise thread firmly against the finished fabric?
75800.e: The reed is a comb-like part that the warp threads run through. You use it to beat each new weft thread into place so that the fabric is dense.
75800.m: The reed beats each weft thread into place.

75801.q: In weaving, what are the lengthways threads called that are stretched tight first?
75801.e: First you stretch the lengthways threads, the warp. Then the crosswise thread, the weft, is passed through again and again.
75801.m: The stretched lengthways threads in weaving are called the warp.

75802.q: In which weave does the crosswise thread always go alternately over one and under one lengthways thread?
75802.e: Plain weave is the simplest and strongest kind of weave. The threads cross at every change.
75802.m: In plain weave, the thread goes over one and under one in turn.

75803.q: Which weave can you recognise by diagonal lines in the fabric, for example in jeans?
75803.e: In twill weave, the crossing points shift by one thread from row to row. This creates a diagonal ridge that is typical of denim.
75803.m: You can recognise twill weave by its diagonal lines.

75804.q: What controlled the patterns on the Jacquard loom around 1805?
75804.e: Joseph-Marie Jacquard from Lyon controlled his loom with punched cards. These cards are seen as early forerunners of computer programming.
75804.m: The Jacquard loom is controlled by punched cards.

75805.q: What is the knitting pattern called where you knit the right-side rows and purl the wrong-side rows?
75805.e: This makes a smooth surface with small V-shaped stitches on the front. On the back you only see purl stitches.
75805.m: Stocking stitch comes from knit rows on the front and purl rows on the back.

75806.q: What are the two basic stitches in knitting?
75806.e: Almost all knitting patterns are made of knit and purl stitches. A knit stitch looks like a purl stitch on the back.
75806.m: The basic stitches in knitting are knit and purl.

75807.q: What is the knitting pattern called where you knit every row with knit stitches only?
75807.e: If you knit only knit stitches there and back, horizontal ridges appear on both sides. This pattern is called garter stitch.
75807.m: Garter stitch comes from knitting every row.

75808.q: What are socks traditionally knitted in the round with?
75808.e: A set of double-pointed needles usually has five short needles with points at both ends. The stitches are spread over four needles and you knit with the fifth.
75808.m: Socks are knitted in the round with double-pointed needles.

75809.q: What do you call finishing a piece of knitting so that the stitches do not come undone?
75809.e: When casting off, you pull each stitch over the next one until only one loop is left. Then the yarn is pulled through and sewn in.
75809.m: At the end, a piece of knitting is cast off.

75810.q: Why is a knitted fabric usually stretchier than a woven fabric?
a: It is made of loops hooked into each other.
It is made only of synthetic fibres.
75810.e: Stitches are loops that can change shape and shift. In a woven fabric, straight threads cross and hardly give at all.
75810.m: Knitting is stretchy because it is made of loops.

75811.q: What do you usually start a piece of crochet with?
75811.e: First you crochet a chain of chain stitches as wide as you want. Then you crochet the first row into this chain.
75811.m: A piece of crochet usually starts with a foundation chain.

75812.q: Which crochet stitch starts by wrapping the yarn once around the hook before inserting it?
75812.e: For a treble, you first wrap the yarn over the hook and then insert it. This makes the stitch taller than a double crochet.
75812.m: A treble starts with a yarn over.

75813.q: How many hooks do you need for crocheting?
75813.e: When crocheting, you work with a single hook. There is only ever one loop left on the hook.
75813.m: You only need one hook for crocheting.

75814.q: Where does the bottom thread on a sewing machine come from?
a: From the bobbin under the needle plate
From the reel of thread at the top
75814.e: The bottom thread is wound onto a small bobbin that sits in the hook under the needle plate. The top thread comes from the reel of thread.
75814.m: The bottom thread comes from the bobbin under the needle plate.

75815.q: What is the basic stitch of a household sewing machine called, where the top and bottom threads loop around each other?
75815.e: In lockstitch, the bottom thread catches the loop of the top thread. The link lies in the middle of the fabric and the seam looks the same on both sides.
75815.m: A sewing machine sews with lockstitch.

75816.q: Which sewing machine stitch is used to finish fabric edges so that they do not fray?
75816.e: Zigzag stitch wraps around the cut edge and holds the threads in place. This stops the fabric fraying.
75816.m: Zigzag stitch is used to finish fabric edges.

75817.q: Which part of the sewing machine moves the fabric along stitch by stitch while sewing?
75817.e: The feed dogs are toothed bars under the presser foot. They move and pull the fabric towards the back.
75817.m: The feed dogs move the fabric along under the presser foot.

75818.q: Where is the eye of a sewing machine needle?
a: At the top by the shank
In the middle of the needle
75818.e: Unlike a hand sewing needle, the eye is just above the point. This allows the top thread to be taken under the fabric.
75818.m: On a sewing machine needle, the eye is near the point.

75819.q: Why do you sew a few stitches backwards at the start and end of a seam?
a: So that the seam does not come undone
So that the needle cools down
75819.e: Sewing backwards locks the threads in place. That way the seam cannot open while the clothes are being worn.
75819.m: Sewing backwards secures the start and end of a seam.

75820.q: Loops of the top thread form on the underside of the fabric. What is usually the cause?
a: The top thread tension is too loose.
75820.e: If the top thread is not tight enough, the bottom thread pulls it down. Often the top thread is also threaded incorrectly.
75820.m: Loops underneath point to a top thread that is too loose.

75821.q: In which century were the first usable sewing machines invented?
75821.e: Around 1830, the Frenchman Barthélemy Thimonnier received a patent for a sewing machine. During the 19th century the machines found their way into factories and homes.
75821.m: The sewing machine was invented in the 19th century.

75822.q: What does the long arrow on a pattern piece show?
75822.e: The arrow must lie parallel to the edge of the fabric along which the lengthways threads run. Then the garment hangs straight and does not twist.
75822.m: The arrow on a pattern piece shows the grain line.

75823.q: What do you call the extra edge of fabric outside the stitching line?
75823.e: The seam allowance is added when cutting out so that you can sew the fabric together. It is often 1 to 1.5 cm wide.
75823.m: Outside the stitching line you need a seam allowance.

75824.q: When cutting out, what does the instruction “place on fold” mean?
a: The piece is placed against the folded edge of the fabric.
The fabric is torn instead of cut.
The piece is placed at a slant.
75824.e: You fold the fabric and place the centre line of the pattern piece on the fold. This creates a symmetrical piece twice as wide with no seam in the middle.
75824.m: A piece cut on the fold is cut along the folded edge.

75825.q: What is a tapering seam called that shapes a garment to the body?
75825.e: A dart takes away fabric in a point. This creates a curve, for example at the waist.
75825.m: Darts shape fabric to the body.

75826.q: What are notches on a sewing pattern for?
75826.e: Notches are small marks on the edges. When the marks on two pieces meet, the pieces are in the right position.
75826.m: Notches show which points belong together.

75827.q: Which tool is used to transfer the lines of a sewing pattern onto fabric with carbon paper?
75827.e: A tracing wheel has a small jagged wheel. You run it along the lines, and the dressmaker's carbon paper presses the line onto the fabric.
75827.m: A tracing wheel transfers pattern lines.

75828.q: Which body measurement do you take at the narrowest part of the torso?
75828.e: The waist is the narrowest point between the ribcage and the hips. You measure it loosely all the way round with a tape measure.
75828.m: You measure the waist at the narrowest part of the torso.

75829.q: What is the turned-up and sewn-down bottom edge of trousers or a skirt called?
75829.e: When hemming, the edge of the fabric is folded over and sewn down. This stops it fraying and gets the length right.
75829.m: The bottom edge of a garment is called the hem.

75830.q: Which of these kinds of wood is a softwood from a conifer?
75830.e: The spruce has needles and cones. Beech, oak and maple are broadleaf trees.

75831.q: Which tree species is the most common in Swiss forests?
75831.e: According to the Swiss National Forest Inventory, the spruce is the most common tree species in Switzerland. Its wood is widely used as building timber.
75831.m: The spruce is the most common tree in Switzerland.

75832.q: What can you tell from the growth rings of a tree trunk?
75832.e: In our climate, a tree forms a light and a dark layer of wood every year. If you count these rings, you know its age.
75832.m: Each growth ring stands for one year of growth.

75833.q: Which very light wood is often used for making models?
75833.e: Balsa wood comes from Central and South America and is one of the lightest timbers. You can even cut it with a knife.
75833.m: Balsa wood is very light and is used for model making.

75834.q: Which conifer wood from the Alps is known for its scent and is often used for living rooms and beds?
75834.e: The Swiss stone pine, also called arolla pine, grows in the Alps up to the tree line. Its wood has a strong scent and is traditionally used in the Engadine for panelled stone pine rooms.
75834.m: Swiss stone pine smells good and is often used for panelled rooms.

75835.q: What is the wood material made of several thin layers of wood glued crosswise called?
75835.e: In plywood, the wood fibres of each layer run across those of the next. This means it hardly warps and is very strong.
75835.m: Plywood is made of layers of wood glued crosswise.

75836.q: Which soft, even wood is especially good for carving?
75836.e: Lime wood is soft, has fine fibres and hardly splinters. Many wooden figures and nativity figures are carved from lime.
75836.m: Lime wood is ideal for carving.

75837.q: How do you fit a blade into a fretsaw?
a: Teeth pointing down towards the handle
Teeth pointing up towards the tip
75837.e: A fretsaw cuts on the downward stroke. That is why the teeth must point down towards the handle.
75837.m: On a fretsaw, the teeth point towards the handle.

75838.q: What is the best thing to rest the workpiece on when using a fretsaw?
a: A fretsaw table with a V-shaped cut-out
75838.e: The small table is screwed onto the workbench. In the V-shaped cut-out you can hold the wood safely and saw.
75838.m: When using a fretsaw, the wood rests on a fretsaw table.

75839.q: How do you move the fretsaw when sawing a curve?
a: Straight up and down, turning the wood
At a slant and fast forwards
75839.e: You hold the saw upright and move it evenly up and down. On curves you slowly turn the workpiece, not the saw.
75839.m: On curves, you turn the wood when using a fretsaw.

75840.q: What do you use a file for in the workshop?
75840.e: A file has lots of small cutting edges on its surface. You use it to remove material and make edges smooth.
75840.m: You smooth and shape edges with a file.

75841.q: In which direction does a file work?
75841.e: The teeth of the file point forwards. That is why you press on the forward stroke and pull the file back without pressure.
75841.m: A file cuts on the forward stroke.

75842.q: Which file-like tool with separate coarse teeth is used for wood?
75842.e: A rasp removes a lot of material at once. Afterwards you smooth the surface with a file and sandpaper.

75843.q: How can you recognise a wood drill bit?
75843.e: A wood drill bit has a small point in the middle. It stops the bit slipping when you start drilling.
75843.m: A wood drill bit has a centre point.

75844.q: How do you set the speed of the drill for a large drill bit?
75844.e: At the edge of a large drill bit, the speed is already high at only a few turns. Too high a speed makes the bit hot and blunt.
75844.m: Large drill bits need a low speed.

75845.q: Which tool makes a cone-shaped recess so that a screw head sits flush?
75845.e: A countersink widens the edge of a drilled hole into a cone shape. A countersunk head then fits exactly and does not stick out.
75845.m: A countersink lets screw heads sit flush.

75846.q: Why do you make a small dent with a centre punch before drilling into metal?
a: So that the drill does not slip
So that the metal becomes softer
So that it is less noisy
So that the metal does not rust
75846.e: The dent guides the tip of the drill to exactly the right spot. Without centre punching, the drill would wander on the smooth surface.
75846.m: Centre punching stops the drill slipping on metal.

75847.q: What do you use to mark lines on metal?
75847.e: A scriber has a hard point and scratches a fine, clearly visible line into the surface. A pencil would not be accurate enough on metal.
75847.m: Lines on metal are marked with a scriber.

75848.q: Which saw is used in the workshop to cut through a metal pipe?
75848.e: A hacksaw has a finely toothed, hardened blade in a frame. It is made for hard materials.
75848.m: Metal is cut with a hacksaw.

75849.q: What is removing sharp edges after sawing metal called?
75849.e: Sawing leaves sharp burrs on the edge. You remove them with a file or deburring tool so that you do not cut yourself.

75850.q: What do you put between the vice and a delicate workpiece so that it does not get marked?
75850.e: The jaws of a vice are ridged and leave marks. Soft jaws made of aluminium, plastic or wood protect the workpiece.
75850.m: Soft jaws stop marks in the vice.

75851.q: What do you do when soldering in electronics?
a: You join metal parts with melted metal
You stick parts together with glue
You weld plastic with a flame
75851.e: The hot soldering iron melts the solder, which is made mainly of tin. It flows around the components and, once it cools, joins them firmly and conductively.
75851.m: When soldering, melted solder joins the metal parts.

75852.q: Which metals is the alloy brass made of?
75852.e: Brass is a golden-yellow alloy of copper and zinc. It is used for brass instruments and door handles, for example.
75852.m: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

75853.q: Which metal is used for cables because it conducts electricity very well?
75853.e: After silver, copper conducts electricity best and is much cheaper. That is why most cable wires are made of copper.
75853.m: Electric cables are usually made of copper.

75854.q: Which of these joints can be undone again without destroying parts?
75854.e: A screw can be unscrewed and put back in. Rivets, glue and welds have to be destroyed to separate the parts.

75855.q: Which rivet can you fit if you can only reach the workpiece from one side?
75855.e: A blind rivet, also called a pop rivet, is set from one side with a rivet gun. The mandrel pulls the rivet together on the back.
75855.m: Blind rivets are set from one side.

75856.q: Which glue is usually used at school for wood joints?
75856.e: PVA glue is a water-based wood glue. It is white when you apply it and becomes almost clear as it dries.
75856.m: Wood is usually glued with PVA glue.

75857.q: What do you use to press freshly glued pieces of wood together until the glue is dry?
75857.e: Glue holds best when the parts are pressed firmly together. Clamps keep up the pressure until the glue has set.

75858.q: Why do you drill a pilot hole before driving a screw into hard wood near the edge?
a: So that the wood does not split
So that the screw gets longer
So that the glue holds better
75858.e: A screw pushes the wood fibres apart. A small pilot hole stops the wood splitting at the edge.
75858.m: Drilling a pilot hole stops wood splitting.

75859.q: What is the spiral groove on a screw called?
75859.e: As you turn the screw, the thread pulls it into the material and holds it tight. A nail has no thread.
75859.m: A screw holds thanks to its thread.

75860.q: What do you put into a drilled hole in a concrete wall so that a screw will hold in it?
75860.e: The plastic wall plug spreads out when the screw is turned in. This way it wedges itself tightly in the hole.
75860.m: In concrete, a screw needs a wall plug.

75861.q: What is a screw head with a six-pointed star-shaped recess usually called?
75861.e: With Torx, the screwdriver grips a star with six rounded points. It slips less easily than a slot.
75861.m: A Torx screw head has a six-pointed star.

75862.q: What is needed for a lamp to light up in an electric circuit?
a: Just one wire to the positive terminal
75862.e: Current only flows if there is an unbroken path from one terminal of the battery through the lamp to the other terminal. Any gap stops the current.
75862.m: Current only flows in a closed circuit.

75863.q: Two lamps are connected in series. What happens if one lamp breaks?
a: The other lamp goes out too.
75863.e: In a series circuit there is only one path for the current. If one lamp fails, the whole circuit is broken.
75863.m: In a series circuit, a broken lamp breaks the whole circuit.

75864.q: In which circuit do the other lamps stay on if one lamp fails?
75864.e: In a parallel circuit, each lamp has its own path for the current. That is why the lights in a flat are also connected in parallel.
75864.m: Lamps connected in parallel work independently of each other.

75865.q: Which of these objects conducts electricity?
75865.e: Metals are good electrical conductors. Rubber, dry wood and plastic are insulators.
75865.m: Metals conduct electricity; plastic and rubber insulate.

75866.q: Which leg of an LED is normally connected to the positive terminal?
75866.e: The longer leg is the anode and goes to positive. An LED only lights up if it is connected the right way round.
75866.m: The longer leg of the LED goes to the positive terminal.

75867.q: Why does an LED on a 9-volt battery need a series resistor?
75867.e: Without a resistor, too much current would flow through the LED and it would be destroyed. The series resistor limits the current to a safe level.
75867.m: A series resistor protects the LED from too much current.

75868.q: What does a switch do in the “off” position?
a: It connects plus and minus directly.
75868.e: In the “off” position, a switch opens a gap in the circuit. Then no more current can flow.
75868.m: An open switch breaks the circuit.

75869.q: What is it called when the positive and negative terminals of a battery are connected directly with a wire?
75869.e: In a short circuit, a lot of current flows without anything using it. The wire and the battery can get hot.
75869.m: A short circuit happens when plus and minus are connected directly.

75870.q: What voltage does a typical flat battery often used in school lessons have?
75870.e: A flat battery contains three cells of 1.5 volts each connected in series. Together that makes 3 times 1.5 V, which is 4.5 V.
75870.m: A flat battery has a voltage of 4.5 volts.

75871.q: What should you always wear when drilling and sanding to protect your eyes?
75871.e: When drilling and sanding, shavings and dust fly off. Safety goggles prevent eye injuries.
75871.m: Safety goggles protect your eyes when drilling and sanding.

75872.q: What must you do with long hair before working at a pillar drill?
a: Nothing, it does not get in the way
75872.e: Loose hair can be caught and wound up by the turning drill spindle. That can lead to serious injuries.
75872.m: Long hair is tied back when using machines.

75873.q: Why do you not wear gloves at a pillar drill?
a: They can get caught by the drill.
They make your hands too warm.
75873.e: A glove can get caught on the turning drill and pull your hand in. That is why gloves are banned at rotating machines.
75873.m: Do not wear gloves at rotating machines.

75874.q: How do you hold a small workpiece when drilling at a pillar drill?
75874.e: The drill can catch and spin the workpiece around. Clamped in a machine vice, it stays safely in place.
75874.m: When drilling, the workpiece is always clamped.

75875.q: Which Swiss institution insures employees against accidents and publishes rules on accident prevention?
75875.e: Suva is the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund, based in Lucerne. It also gives information on working safely in workshops.
75875.m: Suva works for accident prevention in Switzerland.

75876.q: In which direction do you cut with a craft knife or carving knife?
75876.e: If the knife slips, it slides away from your body into empty space. The holding hand stays behind the blade.
75876.m: Always cut away from your body.

75877.q: What do you do if a machine's cable is damaged?
a: Unplug it, do not use it and report it
Wrap it in tape and keep working
75877.e: A damaged cable can cause an electric shock. Only a specialist may repair it.
75877.m: Report damaged cables at once and do not use the machine.

75878.q: Where do you put a hot soldering iron during a break in your work?
75878.e: The tip of a soldering iron is several hundred degrees hot. In the stand, nobody can get burnt and nothing catches fire.
75878.m: A hot soldering iron always goes in its stand.

a: Making a product of higher value from waste
Getting rid of waste at the incineration plant
75879.e: In upcycling, an old object is turned into something new and more valuable. The material is not broken down first.
75879.m: Upcycling turns waste into something more valuable.

75880.q: What is it called when a waste material is turned into a product of lower quality?
75880.e: In downcycling, a material loses quality, for example when office paper becomes cardboard or toilet paper. Afterwards it often cannot be used in the same way again.
75880.m: Downcycling means a material loses value.

a: Sewing a bag from an old pair of jeans
Taking a PET bottle to a collection point
Buying a new pair of jeans
75881.e: The jeans are turned directly into a new, useful object. Handing in PET or paper is part of recycling.
75881.m: A bag made from old jeans is an example of upcycling.

75882.q: Since 1993, which used material has the Zurich company Freitag made bags from?
75882.e: In 1993, the brothers Markus and Daniel Freitag sewed a first bike courier bag from old lorry tarpaulins. It is a well-known Swiss example of upcycling.
75882.m: Freitag bags are made from old lorry tarpaulins.

75883.q: Why is upcycling good for the environment?
a: It saves raw materials and energy.
75883.e: An existing object is used again instead of being thrown away. This means fewer new materials have to be made.
75883.m: Upcycling saves raw materials and energy.

75884.q: What comes first in the waste hierarchy?
75884.e: It is best if no waste is produced at all. Only after that come reusing, recycling and finally burning or landfill.
75884.m: Avoiding waste is better than dealing with it.

75886.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75886.e: This is the flag of Argentina. Argentina is in South America.

75888.e: This is the flag of Australia. Australia is in Oceania.

75891.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?

75892.e: This is the flag of China. Red with one large yellow star and four smaller yellow stars at the top left.

75893.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75893.e: This is the flag of China. China is in Asia.

75894.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75894.e: This is the flag of Germany. Germany is in Europe.

75895.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75895.e: This is the flag of Denmark. Denmark is in Europe.

75896.q: Which country does this flag belong to?
75896.e: This is the flag of Finland. White with a blue Scandinavian cross.

75897.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75897.e: This is the flag of Finland. Finland is in Europe.

75898.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75898.e: This is the flag of France. France is in Europe.

75899.q: Which country does this flag belong to?
75899.e: This is the flag of Greece. Nine horizontal stripes alternating blue and white, with a blue square containing a white cross at the top left.

75900.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75900.e: This is the flag of Greece. Greece is in Europe.

75901.q: Which country does this flag belong to?
75901.e: This is the flag of India. Three horizontal stripes in saffron, white and green, with a blue wheel with 24 spokes (Ashoka Chakra) in the middle.

75902.q: Which continent is the country with this flag in?
75902.e: This is the flag of India. India is in Asia.

75903.q: Which country does this flag belong to?

76430.q: Which fish do these pictures show together?
76430.e: The gold medal stands for gold, and then comes the fish. Together they make goldfish.
76430.m: Goldfish often live in an aquarium or a pond.

76431.q: Which insect do these pictures make?
76431.e: Honey and bee together make honeybee. It collects nectar and turns it into honey.
76431.m: The honeybee makes honey from flower nectar.

76432.q: Which word do these two pictures make?
76432.e: The snail and the house together make snail shell. The snail carries its house, the shell, on its back.
76432.m: The snail shell protects the snail.

76433.q: Which animal from the forest do these pictures show?
76433.e: The fire and the lizard together make fire salamander. It is black with yellow spots.
76433.m: The fire salamander is black with yellow spots.

76437.q: Which drink do these pictures show together?
76437.e: Orange and juice together make orange juice.
76437.m: Orange juice is made from squeezed oranges.

76438.q: Which soup do these pictures show?
76438.e: Tomato and soup together make tomato soup.

76439.q: Which food do these two pictures make?
76439.e: Potato and salad together make potato salad.
76439.m: People like to eat potato salad with sausages.

76441.q: Which ice cream do these pictures show together?
76441.e: Strawberry and ice cream together make strawberry ice cream. In Switzerland, ice cream is called Glace.
76441.m: Strawberry ice cream is pink and tastes of strawberries.

76442.q: Which drink do these pictures show together?
76442.e: Chocolate, which people in Switzerland call Schoggi, and milk together make chocolate milk.
76442.m: Chocolate milk is milk with cocoa.

76443.q: Which cake do these pictures show?
76443.e: Cherry and cake together make cherry cake.
76443.m: For a cherry cake you need ripe cherries.

76444.q: Which drink do these two pictures make?
76444.e: Lemon and tea together make lemon tea.
76444.m: Lemon tea is tea that tastes of lemon.

76445.q: Which vegetable is hidden in these pictures?
76445.e: Flower and cabbage together make cauliflower, which means ‘cabbage flower’. Its white head looks like a big blossom.
76445.m: Cauliflower is a vegetable with a white head.

76446.q: Which clock hangs in the room? Which word do the pictures show?
76446.e: The wall and the clock together make wall clock.
76446.m: A wall clock hangs on the wall.

76447.q: Which thing at the house is meant here?
76447.e: Letter and box together make letterbox. The postman puts the letters in there.
76447.m: The post is in the letterbox.

76448.q: What do visitors press before they come in?
76448.e: The door and the bell together make doorbell.
76448.m: When visitors come, the doorbell rings.

76449.q: Which thing for at home do these pictures show?
76449.e: House and key together make house key.
76449.m: You unlock the front door with the house key.

76450.q: Where does this animal like to sleep? Which word do the pictures show?
76450.e: Cat and basket together make cat basket.
76450.m: In the cat basket, the cat can curl up and sleep.

76452.q: What do you put flowers in with water? Which word do the pictures show?
76452.e: The flowers and the container that looks like a vase together make flower vase.
76452.m: Cut flowers stay fresh in a flower vase.

76453.q: What is on every house? Which word do the pictures show?
76453.e: House and number together make house number. The digits stand for the number.
76453.m: The house number helps the post find the right house.

76454.q: What do you colour with at school? Which word do the pictures show?
76454.e: The colours and the pencil together make coloured pencil. In Switzerland, it is called a Farbstift.
76454.m: You draw colourful pictures with coloured pencils.

76455.q: Which outing with the class do these pictures show?
76455.e: School and the suitcase, which stands for a trip, together make school trip.
76455.m: On a school trip, the whole class goes on an outing.

76458.e: Colouring and book together make colouring book.
76458.m: In a colouring book you can colour in pictures.

76459.q: What rings at school? Which word do the pictures show?
76459.e: School and bell together make school bell.
76459.m: The school bell shows when break starts and ends.

76460.q: Which school word do these two pictures make?
76460.e: The house stands for home, and the tasks stand for work. Together they make homework, which you do at home.
76460.m: You do your homework at home after school.

76461.q: Which device can you do sums with? Which word do the pictures show?
76461.e: The pocket and the calculating device together make pocket calculator.
76461.m: With a pocket calculator you can do sums quickly.

76462.q: Which toy do these pictures make together?
76462.e: Doll and house together make dolls’ house.
76462.m: Little dolls live in a dolls’ house.

76463.q: Where do children like to play? Which word do the pictures show?
76463.e: Sand and box together make sandbox.
76463.m: In the sandbox you can bake cakes out of sand.

76465.q: What can you shake to make it snow inside? Which word do the pictures show?
76465.e: Snow and the ball, or globe, together make snow globe.
76465.m: When you shake a snow globe, snow swirls around inside.

76466.q: Which castle do children play with? Which word do the pictures show?
76466.e: The swords stand for the knights, and then comes the castle. Together they make knights’ castle.
76466.m: Knights live in a knights’ castle.

76467.q: Which toy do these pictures show together?
76467.e: Wood and horse together make wooden horse.
76467.m: A wooden horse is a toy horse made of wood.

76468.q: Which ball game do these two pictures make?
76468.e: Foot and ball together make football.
76468.m: In football you play the ball with your foot.

76471.q: What do you put on your feet when it rains? Which word do the pictures show?
76471.e: Rain and boots together make rain boots.
76471.m: In rain boots you can walk through puddles.

76472.q: Which cloud brings lightning and thunder? Which word do the pictures show?
76472.e: The lightning stands for thunder, and then comes the cloud. Together they make thundercloud.
76472.m: Lightning and thunder come from a thundercloud.

76474.q: What gathers in the sky before it gets wet? Which word do the pictures show?
76474.e: The water drop stands for rain, and then comes the cloud. Together they make rain cloud.
76474.m: Rain will soon fall from a dark rain cloud.

76476.q: What shows on television what the weather will be like? Which word do the pictures show?
76476.e: The weather and the map together make weather map.
76476.m: On the weather map you can see sun, clouds and rain.

76477.q: What do you call a day when it rains? Which word do the pictures show?
76477.e: Rain and day together make rainy day. The calendar stands for the day.
76477.m: On a rainy day, people like to stay indoors.

76478.q: Which vehicle brings parcels? Which word do the pictures show?
76478.e: The parcel stands for delivery, and then comes the van. Together they make delivery van.
76478.m: A delivery van brings parcels and goods.

76480.q: Which car is meant by these pictures?
76480.e: The police officer and the car together make police car.
76480.m: A police car has a blue light and a siren.

76481.q: Which vehicle for space do these pictures show?
76481.e: Moon and rocket together make moon rocket. People flew to the Moon in rockets.
76481.m: In 1969, people landed on the Moon for the first time.

76482.q: What flies to injured people in the mountains? Which word do the pictures show?
76482.e: The ambulance stands for rescue, and then comes the helicopter. Together they make rescue helicopter.
76482.m: In Switzerland, rescue helicopters fly injured people to hospital.

76483.q: Which aeroplane can land on a lake? Which word do the pictures show?
76483.e: The water and the aeroplane together make seaplane, a plane for the water.
76483.m: A seaplane can land on water.

76485.q: Which ship is meant by these pictures?
76485.e: The steam and the ship together make steamship.
76485.m: Old steamships still sail on several Swiss lakes.

76486.q: Which fast car do these pictures show?
76486.e: Racing and car together make racing car.
76486.m: A racing car goes very fast on a racetrack.

76487.q: What keeps your head warm in winter? Which word do the pictures show?
76487.e: The wool and the hat together make woolly hat.
76487.m: A woolly hat keeps your head warm.

76488.q: Which piece of clothing do these pictures show?
76488.e: Rain and coat together make raincoat.
76488.m: A raincoat keeps us dry in the rain.

76489.q: What do you wear on your nose in summer? Which word do the pictures show?
76489.e: Sun and glasses together make sunglasses.
76489.m: Sunglasses protect your eyes from bright light.

76493.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
76493.e: Trousers and pocket together make trouser pocket.
76493.m: You can carry small things in your trouser pocket.

76494.q: Which shoes do you need for PE? Which word do the pictures show?
76494.e: Gym and shoe together make gym shoe.
76494.m: You wear gym shoes for PE.

76495.q: Which doctor looks after children? Which word do the pictures show?
76495.e: The child and the doctor’s stethoscope together make children’s doctor.
76495.m: The children’s doctor examines children who are ill.

76496.q: What do you put on your toothbrush when you brush your teeth? Which word do the pictures show?
76496.e: Tooth and paste together make toothpaste. It goes on the toothbrush.
76496.m: You need toothpaste to brush your teeth.

76497.q: What do you have when a baby tooth is missing? Which word do the pictures show?
76497.e: The tooth and the hole together make a gap in your teeth.
76497.m: When a baby tooth falls out, you have a gap in your teeth.

76498.q: Which word for a song you cannot forget do these pictures show?
76498.e: Ear and worm together make earworm. An earworm is a song you cannot get out of your head.
76498.m: An earworm is a song that keeps going round in your head.

76499.q: What protects your ears in winter? Which word do the pictures show?
76499.e: The ear and the shield, which protects, together make earmuffs.

76501.q: What do you paint with without a brush? Which word do the pictures show?
76501.e: Finger and paint together make finger paint. With it, you paint directly with your fingers.
76501.m: With finger paint you paint with your fingers.

76502.q: Which jewellery do these pictures make?
76502.e: Ear and ring together make earring.
76502.m: You wear an earring as jewellery on your ear.

76503.q: Where do lots of flowers grow next to each other in the garden? Which word do the pictures show?
76503.e: Flower and bed together make flower bed. A bed is a patch of soil in the garden where you plant things.
76503.m: Flowers grow in the flower bed.

76504.q: Which plant in the meadow do these pictures show?
76504.e: Lion and tooth together make dandelion: the name comes from French ‘dent de lion’, lion’s tooth. Its leaves have points like teeth.
76504.m: The dandelion has bright yellow flowers.

76505.q: What do birds bathe in in the garden? Which word do the pictures show?
76505.e: Bird and bath together make birdbath.
76505.m: Birds can drink and bathe in the birdbath.

76506.q: What do you use to cut off twigs in the garden? Which word do the pictures show?
76506.e: Garden and scissors together make garden shears.
76506.m: You cut twigs and flowers with garden shears.

76507.q: What do you go through to get into the garden? Which word do the pictures show?
76507.e: The garden and the football goal, which stands for a gate, together make garden gate.
76507.m: You get into the garden through the garden gate.

76509.q: Which tree is meant by these pictures?
76509.e: Apple and tree together make apple tree.
76509.m: Apples grow on an apple tree.

76511.q: What do you rake together in autumn? Which word do the pictures show?
76511.e: The leaves and the mountain, which stands for a pile, together make pile of leaves.
76511.m: In autumn the leaves fall, and you rake them into a pile of leaves.

76513.q: Where do you go ice skating in winter? Which word do the pictures show?
76513.e: Ice and the track, a rink, together make ice rink.
76513.m: In winter you can go ice skating at the ice rink.

76514.q: What stops you sinking into deep snow? Which word do the pictures show?
76514.e: Snow and shoe together make snowshoe.
76514.m: With snowshoes you can walk in deep snow.

76516.q: What does this animal do in the cold season? Which word do the pictures show?
76516.e: The snow stands for winter, and then comes the sleeping hedgehog. Together they show a long winter sleep, called hibernation.
76516.m: The hedgehog hibernates for a long time in winter.

76517.q: What protects your head in summer? Which word do the pictures show?
76517.e: Sun and hat together make sun hat.
76517.m: A sun hat protects your head from the sun.

76518.q: What do children use to splash each other in summer? Which word do the pictures show?
76518.e: Water and balloon together make water balloon.
76518.m: A water balloon bursts and makes you wet.

76519.q: What lights up the sky on the national holiday? Which word do the pictures show?
76519.e: The fire and the factory, which is also called works, together make fireworks.
76519.m: On 1 August there are often fireworks in Switzerland.

76520.q: What do you wrap presents in? Which word do the pictures show?
76520.e: The present and the paper together make wrapping paper.
76520.m: You wrap presents nicely in wrapping paper.

76521.q: What hangs on the wall at a party? Which word do the pictures show?
76521.e: The air and the balloon belong together: a balloon is filled with air.
76521.m: You blow up a balloon with air.

76522.q: What do you blow out on your birthday? Which word do the pictures show?
76522.e: The birthday cake and the candle together make birthday candle.
76522.m: Birthday candles burn on the birthday cake.

76523.q: Who brings presents at Christmas in stories? Which word do the pictures show?
76523.e: The Christmas tree stands for Christmas, and then comes the man, the father. Together they make Father Christmas.
76523.m: Father Christmas wears a red coat and has a white beard.

76524.q: Which cake belongs to this celebration? Which word do the pictures show?
76524.e: The chapel stands for a wedding, and then comes the cake. Together they make wedding cake.
76524.m: A wedding cake often has several tiers.

76525.q: Where do lots of people celebrate together? Which word do the pictures show?
76525.e: The festival and the tent together make festival tent.
76525.m: Lots of people celebrate together in a festival tent.

76526.q: What makes the living room cosy at Christmas? Which word do the pictures show?
76526.e: Candle and light together make candlelight.
76526.m: Candlelight makes a room warm and cosy.

76527.q: What do you put on your head at a party? Which word do the pictures show?
76527.e: The party and the hat together make party hat.
76527.m: You wear a party hat at a birthday party, for example.

76528.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76528.e: The cow eats grass, gives milk that is made into butter, and often wears a bell.
76528.m: The cow gives us milk and eats grass.

76529.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76529.e: The hen has feathers and lays eggs, which you can fry, for example.

76530.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76530.e: The sheep’s wool is made into yarn, and socks and scarves are knitted from it.

76531.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76531.e: Bacon and many sausages are made from pork. The pig likes to roll in brown mud to cool down.
76531.m: The pig likes to wallow in mud.

76532.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76532.e: You can ride a horse like a cowboy. It likes to eat hay, and an apple as a treat.
76532.m: You can ride on a horse.

76533.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76533.e: The cockerel crows loudly early in the morning, almost like an alarm clock.
76533.m: The cockerel crows in the morning.

76534.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76534.e: The goat often has a beard, gives milk and likes to climb around in the mountains.
76534.m: The goat likes to climb and often has a beard.

76535.q: Which farm animal goes with these pictures?
76535.e: The cat creeps on quiet paws and often hunts mice at night, on the farm too.

76536.q: Which forest animal goes with these pictures?
76536.e: The squirrel often has reddish-brown fur, climbs trees and hides nuts for the winter.
76536.m: The squirrel hides nuts for the winter.

76537.q: Which forest bird goes with these pictures?
76537.e: The cuckoo calls its own name, like the cuckoo clock. It lays its eggs in other birds’ nests.
76537.m: The cuckoo lays its eggs in other birds’ nests.

76538.q: Which forest animal goes with these pictures?
76538.e: The owl has big eyes and hunts in the forest at night.
76538.m: The owl is awake at night.

76539.q: Which forest animal goes with these pictures?
76539.e: The woodpecker hammers its beak into the wood of trees. The great spotted woodpecker has red feathers.
76539.m: The woodpecker knocks on trees with its beak.

76540.q: Which forest animal goes with these pictures?
76540.e: The bat is out and about at night, sleeps hanging upside down and finds its way with its ears.

76541.q: Which forest animal goes with these pictures?
76541.e: In German, this animal is called the ‘seven sleeper’. It hibernates for a long time, often seven months or longer.
76541.m: The edible dormouse sleeps for a very long time in winter.

76542.q: Which bird from the forest and garden goes with these pictures?
76542.e: The robin has an orange-red breast. It often stays with us in winter too.
76542.m: The robin has an orange-red breast.

76543.q: Which forest animal goes with these pictures?
76543.e: A young roe deer is called a fawn. It has brown fur with white spots and hides in the forest and in the meadow.
76543.m: A young roe deer is called a fawn.

76544.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76544.e: The octopus has eight arms and squirts black ink into the water when it is in danger.

76545.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76545.e: The starfish looks like a star and usually has five arms, just as a hand has five fingers.
76545.m: The starfish usually has five arms.

76546.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76546.e: The shark has lots of sharp teeth. You often see its triangular dorsal fin sticking out of the water.
76546.m: The shark has a triangular dorsal fin.

76547.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76547.e: The dolphin looks as if it is smiling, likes to jump out of the water and is very clever.
76547.m: The dolphin is a clever sea creature.

76548.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76548.e: The whale is huge; some are longer than a bus. When it breathes out, it blows a spout into the air.
76548.m: The whale blows a spout when it breathes out.

76549.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76549.e: The crab has pincers, lives by the sea and on the beach, and usually walks sideways.

76550.q: Which sea creature goes with these pictures?
76550.e: The seal eats fish, likes to lie on the ice and sometimes slaps its flippers as if it were clapping.
76550.m: The seal likes to eat fish.

76551.e: The clownfish is orange with white stripes, as colourful as a clown. It lives in sea anemones.
76551.m: The clownfish has orange and white stripes.

76552.e: When it is in danger, the pufferfish blows itself up into a ball like a balloon.
76552.m: The pufferfish can blow itself up into a ball.

76553.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76553.e: The bee has yellow and black stripes, flies to flowers and makes honey.

76554.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76554.e: After a while, the caterpillar turns into a butterfly with colourful wings.
76554.m: A caterpillar turns into a butterfly.

76555.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76555.e: The ladybird is red with black spots and is thought to bring good luck.
76555.m: The ladybird is thought to bring good luck.

76556.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76556.e: Wood ants build big mounds out of pine needles. Ants are very strong and carry much more than their own weight.
76556.m: For its size, the ant is very strong.

76557.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76557.e: The flea is so small you can hardly see it. It lives in the fur of dogs, for example, and can jump very far.
76557.m: The flea can jump very far.

76558.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76558.e: The dragonfly flies like a helicopter and can stay still in the air. It likes to live near water.
76558.m: The dragonfly can stay still in the air.

76559.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76559.e: The cricket chirps in the meadow in the evening. It makes its music by rubbing its wings together.
76559.m: The cricket chirps in the meadow.

76560.q: Which insect goes with these pictures?
76560.e: The bumblebee is fat and furry like a soft toy and buzzes from flower to flower.
76560.m: The bumblebee is fat and furry.

76561.e: The plum is purple and ripens in late summer and autumn. In Switzerland, people bake a delicious plum tart with it.
76561.m: Plums are used to bake a tart.

76562.e: The blueberry is blue, grows in the forest and turns your tongue blue when you eat it.

76563.e: The kiwi is brown and hairy on the outside and green on the inside. You can scoop it out with a spoon.
76563.m: The kiwi is green on the inside.

76564.e: The lemon is yellow and so sour that it makes you pull a face. Lemonade is made from it.
76564.m: The lemon is yellow and sour.

76565.e: The banana is yellow and curved like a moon, and monkeys love eating it.
76565.m: The banana is yellow and curved.

76566.e: The pineapple has leaves on top like a crown, is yellow inside, grows in warm countries and goes on a Hawaiian pizza.
76566.m: The pineapple has a tuft of leaves on top like a crown.

76567.e: The coconut grows on palm trees, is brown and hairy on the outside and has coconut water inside.
76567.m: The coconut grows on palm trees.

76568.e: After the blossoms, red cherries grow on the cherry tree, often in pairs on one stalk.
76568.m: Cherries often hang in pairs on the tree.

76569.e: A light bulb is shaped like a pear; in German, both are called ‘Birne’. The tree shows that a fruit is meant.
76569.m: The pear grows on a tree.

76570.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76570.e: In the fairy tale, the princess feels a small green pea under lots of mattresses.
76570.m: The pea is small, round and green.

76571.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76571.e: Chips are made from potatoes. The potato is brown on the outside and grows under the ground.

76572.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76572.e: You need red tomatoes for the sauce on pizza and with spaghetti.
76572.m: Red sauce is made from tomatoes.

76573.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76573.e: Cutting onions often brings tears to your eyes. The onion has a brown skin and goes into lots of soups.
76573.m: Cutting onions often makes you cry.

76574.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76574.e: You eat green cucumber in salad. For beauty care, some people put cucumber slices on their eyes.
76574.m: The cucumber is green and crunchy.

76575.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76575.e: At Halloween, the orange pumpkin becomes a lantern with a candle. You can also make soup from it.
76575.m: You can carve a lantern out of a pumpkin.

76576.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76576.e: Sweetcorn has yellow kernels and grows in fields. Popcorn is made from corn kernels.
76576.m: Popcorn is made from corn kernels.

76577.q: Which vegetable goes with these pictures?
76577.e: Green broccoli looks like lots of little trees.
76577.m: Broccoli looks like a little tree.

76578.q: Which break-time snack goes with these pictures?
76578.e: The croissant is curved like a half moon, is baked with lots of butter and tastes good in the morning. In Switzerland it is called a Gipfeli.
76578.m: The croissant is curved like a half moon.

76579.q: Which break-time snack goes with these pictures?
